For the heavens of heavens already praise her, as do the sun and moon, the stars and the light, the whole world, choirs and legions of angels, and all the hosts of heavenly spirits.

Therefore, inspired by the Holy Spirit, the holy men of God from every nation under heaven have attempted to exalt her with wondrous praises, gilded expressions, and radiant and splendid discourses. But I, to whom gifts of grace have not been given so abundantly and splendidly, shall illuminate her from the little spark infused into me—or, as far as I can, though stammering in a little vernacular, shall display her—lest I be found ungrateful for having tasted her abundance.

[Note: [Col. 0286B] Alva printed *vernulam*, wrongly; we have corrected it from the manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0285B] “Radiance” is absent from Alva’s edition.]

[Note: [Col. 0285B] We add “holy” from our manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0285B] Alva has “almost all,” *omnis*.]

So that, in accordance with the word quoted above, her most holy head may shine with more ample adornment, I place upon it a certain golden crown marked with twelve stones, splendid with six brilliant lights, fragrant with six most beautiful flowers, and sprinkled with every sweetness.

[Note: [Col. 0286B] Alva has “lights,” *lucibus*.]

The order of its arrangement will contain the following sequence: in the first place I shall set topaz; in the second, lucan; in the third, sardius; in the fourth, lily; in the fifth, chalcedony; in the sixth, Arcturus; in the seventh, sapphire; in the eighth, saffron; in the ninth, agate; in the tenth, the maritime star; in the eleventh, jasper; in the twelfth, rose; in the thirteenth, carbuncle; in the fourteenth, the sun; in the fifteenth, emerald; in the sixteenth, violet; in the seventeenth, amethyst; in the eighteenth, the moon; in the nineteenth, chrysolite; in the twentieth, heliotrope; in the twenty-first, chrysoprase; in the twenty-second, Orion; in the twenty-third, beryl; in the twenty-fourth, chamomile.

Thus the crown may be made more nobly distinguished, beautified, and adorned by precious stones, shining lights, and beautiful flowers, and may be received more pleasingly and joyfully by the Lady.

Therefore I ask you, life-giving Virgin, most pure, sincere, and radiant, most noble Queen, to accept this very small service graciously; receive me into your grace and under your protection, and, once delivered from every danger, join me one day to the angelic choirs.

I ask that you show yourself gracious and serene to the children of grace who glorify you here or seek your help. By your intercession may they deserve forgiveness of their sins; under your guidance may they reach the glory of paradise. Amen.

The prologue ends.

## CHAPTER ONE. Why this crown ought to belong to Our Lady

In the longing of my soul, in the joy of the Holy Spirit, in sincere charity, and in the word of truth, I desire to exalt you, praise you, and bless you, Virgin more beautiful than the sun, fairer to behold, greener with faith and grace; since you are most beautiful, serene, bright, radiant, and lovely, lovable as a rose, pleasing, gracious, and splendid.

Yet your dignity and excellence are so great that, even if I were to speak in the tongues of human beings and angels in order to praise and glorify you, and knew all the secrets of the mysteries and possessed all the knowledge of the Scriptures, my strength and power would fail before the beginnings of so many praises could be fully explained.

For you are incomparable among all women in beauty, adornment, and elegance; brighter than all human beings in virtue, grace, and wisdom; more glorious than the angels in the eminence of dignity, the excellence of holiness, and the attainment of glory and honor.

[Note: [Col. 0287D] Where the manuscript reads “holiness,” Alva repeats “dignity.”]

Exalted above the choirs of angels, above the thrones of the apostles and prophets, and above all the citizens of heaven, you sit crowned at the right hand of your most loving Son. There your merits are recited; your praises are gloriously exalted; your commendations and prerogatives are proclaimed reverently and most devoutly by all.

What, then, can I, miserable and sinful as I am, add to such ineffable things? My pen is led here only for this purpose: that some small drop of your praise may be directed there.

This crown that I promise you, Lady, ought rightly to be golden. For just as gold surpasses every kind of metal, so you, Lady, hold sovereignty over all in heaven and on earth.

Every knee of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth bows to you, and every tongue confesses that you are the Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the glory of God the Father, clothed with the sun as with a garment, crowned with a splendid garland of twelve stars, and adorned with glory and radiance. And just as gold is conspicuous in brightness and beautiful in form, so you, Lady, are most radiant in holiness, most brilliant in virtues and miracles, most radiant in illustrious merits, and beautiful and splendid in mind and body.

## PRAYER

Virgin Queen, clothed with the sun, crowned with twelve stars, exalted in heaven, since you are compassionate and more tender-hearted than all, more serene than the star of the sea, look upon the hostile arrows with which I am pierced; behold the sorrows by which I am tormented; see the temptations by which I am battered.

May the enemy not rage for long, may he not overthrow or subject me; may your right hand cast him down and may hell swallow him. And so that the eye of faith may not grow dim in death, may the ray of your brightness then shine upon me.

While hard and bitter death destroys the body, while past evils trouble the mind, while the whole conscience trembles, may your presence assist us; and so that we may not be disturbed by our adversaries, defend us with your protections.

May we pass safely, with the hope of the holy resurrection, assured of the glory of everlasting brightness. Amen.

## CHAPTER TWO. The precious stone topaz in the Virgin’s crown
[Note: [Col. 0287D] Alva printed *omni* (“every”),] Virgin full of every grace, wholly bright and serene, holy and blessed resting-place, golden and translucent, fitted out for the beauty and glory of the Son of God, to the praise and glory of your excellence, in the first place of your illustrious crown I fasten the Topaz, a stone surpassing the brilliance of all stones [Note: [Col. 0287D] Alva incorrectly printed *imperantem* (“ruling”).]; it rightly belongs to the adornment of your noble crown, since, most sweet Lady, just as you surpass all women in the beauty of the flesh, so you surpass all saints and all [Col. 0287D] angels in the excellence of holiness.

For your whole life was an exemplar of holiness and perfection to everyone, and a regulated discipline of conduct. If someone is commended for faith, who is richer in it than you? If in hope, who is more long-suffering? If in charity, who is more fervent? In religious devotion, who is more upright? Who more diligent in reading? Who more devout in prayer? Who more discerning in contemplation? Who more compassionate in pity? Who gentler in mildness? Who purer in chastity? Who cleaner in virginity and temperance? Who [Col. 0288A] richer in knowledge? Who more eloquent in justice? Who stronger against adversity? What saint or angel has penetrated the divine mysteries more deeply? Who has drawn divine grace to himself more abundantly? Who has contemplated the highest majesty more clearly and transparently?

Rightly, therefore, Lady, you possess the Topaz in the adornment of your head, superior to all stones, because you surpass all saints and angels in the beauty of virtues, the splendor of spiritual gifts, and the crowns of merits. Therefore, because of the beauty of all the good things you possess and the overflowing abundance of your entire mercy, you draw sinners to pardon, lead fighters to the crown of the prize, and guide the just to incorruptible glory.

You, Lady of the world, queen of heaven, removed servitude, restored freedom, took away death, and gave life when you bore our Savior, the Son of God. You, Lady, refresh us in difficulties, strengthen us in adversity, fortify us in weakness, free us in death, rescue us from demons, [Col. 0288B] withdraw us from everlasting death, open for us the gate of paradise, and join us to our Redeemer. You, mother of indulgence, loose what is bound, unfasten what has been loosened, mitigate adversity, heal the contrite, absolve the guilty, restore offenders, raise up the fallen, revive the despairing, renew honor, restore confidence, and pour in strength and grace. You restrain indignation, restore the lost inheritance, separate us from the devil, purify us from sin, and reconcile us to God.

## Prayer

O [Note: [Col. 0287D] *Virga aurea* (“golden rod”), manuscript.] golden Virgin, holiest Mother of God, the angels’ rejoicing, the patriarchs’ exultation, the prophets’ joy, the apostles’ delight, the martyrs’ sweetness, the confessors’ savor, the virgins’ harmony: incline your merciful ears toward me and turn those merciful eyes of yours toward me. I am blind: pour light into me. I am infirm: grant me health. I am dead: give me life.

For at your honey-sweet glance the groaning rejoice; at your gentlest touch the sick are healed [Note: [Col. 0287D] Alva: “most lightly”]; and by your rose-like fragrance [Col. 0288C] the dead revive. Everything good that takes place in heaven is either bestowed through your merits or obtained through your prayers.

Look, then, Lady, upon this wretched sinner, darkened by sins and surrounded by many miseries. Through you, holiest Virgin, may my bonds be broken, my debts forgiven, my ruins repaired, my old things renewed, my broken things strengthened, my losses restored, and my imperfections perfected. By your grace may my will be cleansed, my mind shine forth, my spirit be kindled, my breast melt, my taste grow sweet, and my appearance be adorned.

Help me, lamp by which I am illuminated; sweetness by which I am refreshed; power by which I am strengthened; fortitude by which I am sustained. Keep far from me an iniquitous and deceitful word, a wicked thought [Note: [Col. 0287D] “Wicked” is absent from Alva’s edition], and a detestable deed. May your grace direct my entire life; may your presence enlighten my mind; may your mercy lead me to eternal life.

For truly you are [Note: [Col. 0287D] This passage is corrupt here, no less in our manuscript than in Alva’s edition. First, both read *vita* (“life”), where *via* (“way”) should plainly be written; next, as the passage is joined here, it means nothing, nor does *sinitur*—the reading we find in our manuscript. Finally, Alva conjectures that *amatur* should be read for *O Mater!* (“O Mother!”), but this too does not clarify the meaning of the sentence.] the straight way to that glory, as the passage is joined here. O Mother, by whom one advances toward the summit of heaven, through you this assembly of the humble is received here.

Honeycomb and honey of sweetness, and the whiteness of a flower; mistress of the world, bond of charity, joining of love, cleansing sins; virginal dignity adorned with the lily, fruitful virginity exalted upon the throne; queen of angels, medicine of salvation, flower of the valleys; discipline of virtues, curtain of purity, light of hearts; supernatural queen, worldly [Note: [Col. 0288D] We supplied *mundialis* (“worldly”) from the manuscript; it is certainly required for the rhyme.] keel, throne of Christ: lead with you the little ones [*parvulos?*] to the glory of the saints after exile [Note: [Col. 0288D] *Post* (“after”) is absent from Alva’s edition]. Amen.

## Chapter III. The star Lucanum occupies the second place in the Virgin’s crown

[Col. 0289A]

Therefore, illustrious Virgin, blessed gate of heaven, delight of paradise, lady of the angels, queen of the world, joy of the saints; advocate of believers, strength of fighters, restorer of the wandering, remedy of penitents: to the praise and glory of your imperial majesty, in the second place of your glorious crown I fasten Lucanum.

Lucanum is a spherical and round body, bright and shining, beautiful and gracious; all these qualities, holiest Lady, greatly suit you, and therefore it rightly ought to be placed in your crown. In a circular and round form eternity is signified, having neither beginning nor end. For although you, Lady, began to exist in time, [Note: [Col. 0289D] This passage is corrupt in Alva’s edition: “*Corona Deo quodammodo aeterna Deo extitisti*” (“A crown: to God, in some way eternal; to God you existed”).] you existed in some way eternally before God, since you had been eternally foreordained by his majesty, [Note: [Col. 0289D] At this point the manuscript inserts: “known and foreordained from the beginning and before the ages.”] chosen before the foundation of the world [Col. 0289B] as the holy and immaculate Mother of God, so that through you God might send us his peace from heaven, redeem the human race, repair the angelic fall, lead the fettered out from the prison of hell, and open the gate of heaven.

You were also bright in holy works, brighter in saving examples, and brightest in glorious merits. Before God and human beings you were lovable and pleasing, most gracious above the beauty of women, most elegant above the beauty of angels.

O how great you are in merits, Mother of God! O how great is the sweetness of your pity and mercy! You repair earthly things, restore heavenly things, join the lowest to the highest, and mercifully dispense grace to all who cry out to you.

Therefore, let whoever needs mercy approach you, and he will find your compassion overflowing with mercy. Let whoever, driven by the opposing side, doubts in faith look to you, and what was wavering will be firmly established. Let whoever is enticed by carnal desire invoke your grace, and the danger to chastity will be removed. Let whoever is assailed in mind by pride and arrogance turn his gaze toward you, [Col. 0289C] and through the merit of your humility the swelling of his spirit will subside. Let whoever is inflamed by the torches of anger raise his eyes to you, and through your tranquility he will become gentle. Let whoever has been led astray from the way of life through error look to you, Star of the Sea, and in your light he will be led back to the path of truth.

Your piety comes to the aid of every danger and is powerful to do so. And rightly, since you are Mother of God, queen of the world, empress of the heavens, bride of the Holy Spirit. For you cause people to remain in Christ and attain divine things. You flourish in the eternity of God, shine in the truth of God, and rejoice in the goodness of God. You restore those separated from vices to grace, join them to holiness, drive away crimes, wash away faults; you restore innocence to the fallen and joy to the sorrowful; you drive away hatred and prepare concord. You restrain wars, suppress anger, trample the proud, love the humble, calm the discordant, reconcile enemies, unite those present, invite those absent, and reconcile earthly things with heavenly and the lowest with divine things.

You bore the God of heaven, the king of earth, the Lord of the world, [Col. 0289D] the restorer of the world, the slayer of death, the restorer of life, the author of perpetuity. In conceiving him you felt no lust, nor in giving birth did you feel pain.

For this blessed birth I offer this song of praise:

> O nurturing Creator of the stars,  
> Born before Lucifer,  
> Desiring to save the world,  
> At the evening of this world  
> He enters the womb of brightness,  
> Like a bridegroom coming forth.  
>
> He is proclaimed through the prophets,  
> Shown forth in figures,  
> This great mystery.  
>
> Through Gabriel’s oracle,  
> Brought from heaven to Mary,  
> The glorious sign is made known.  
>
> Just as a pleasing fragrance  
> Is emitted from a flower or lily,  
> So from Mary’s womb  
> The Father’s Word is emitted.  
>
> The glory of fruitfulness  
> And the honor of virginity  
> In Mary’s body,  
> As whiteness remains in the rose  
> And beautiful brightness  
> Is displayed in ivory.

Therefore, since after God you are the cause of all good things, I long and desire to praise you, to love your beauty, to venerate your blessedness, to glorify your sublimity, and to implore your goodness.

## Prayer

[Col. 0290B] Pour down, therefore, from above the light of your compassion, so that my soul, filthy with sins, may be cleansed by your grace, illumined by your glory, sweetened by your sweetness, inflamed by your love, and preserved by your protection.

May your virginal and divine birth [Note: [Col. 0289D] “Your” is absent from Alva’s edition] redeem me, a captive; heal me, a sick man; enlighten me, a blind man; raise me, a dead man; and guard me from every sin and danger.

My Lady, whom I shall honor; my sweetness, whom I shall love; my queen, whom I shall revere; my bride, to whom I shall devote myself: turn the grace of your countenance upon me, so that in your beauty I may see light, amid darkness see truth, amid vanity see life, and avoid death.

Since you are fullest of every grace, cleanse my inward parts from all wickedness, make my heart a temple of God, and fill it with your holy love, so that in loving you I may desire you, in desiring you seek you, in seeking find you, in finding embrace and hold you, and in you [Note: [Col. 0290D] Where our manuscript has *suaviter* (“sweetly”), Alva reads *sua vita* (“her life”).] sweetly rest.

## Chapter IV. In the third place the Sardius stone is placed in the Virgin’s crown

[Col. 0290C]

Virgin, mother of pity, throne of the highest majesty, whom the nature of angels and human beings serves, whom every creature praises with one voice; at whose nod dry things become moist, cold things grow warm, and dead things revive; whose life is holier than anything, whose conscience purer than anything, whose kisses happier than anything, whose love more honorable than anything, whose embrace chaster than anything, whose dowry more useful than anything:

Because I, a sinner, see such things in you and desire to please you and, in a manner, applaud you, so that your crown may shine more brilliantly, in its third place I set the precious Sardius stone [Note: [Col. 0290D] *Colloco* (“I place”) is absent from Alva’s edition], adorned with a purple brilliance.

The Sardius, therefore, illumines your noble crown with its red brilliance, since it colors and dyes your spirit purple with spiritual martyrdom. For when your most loving Son, the bridegroom of your virginity, is bound and beaten with scourges, mocked with spittle, assailed with insults, wearied by reproaches, dishonored by mockery, fastened to the cross with nails, given gall [Col. 0290D] and vinegar to drink, and pierced in the side by a lance, you become wholly undone, exhausted by every sorrow, tortured by every pain, tormented by every torment, and embittered by every bitterness. You are wounded in mind, pierced through in soul, struck by a dart in the heart, stabbed in the breast, martyred by the sword, and wholly slaughtered in your inmost parts.

But now rejoice, Lady, because the one whom you saw dying on earth you now behold reigning in heaven. He makes you, who shared in his sorrows, a companion there of his glory and joy, granting you perpetual honor, so that every knee may bend to you and every tongue confess praises to you, [Note: [Col. 0290D] “As Mother of God.” Alva printed *antequam* (“before”), but conjectured that *tanquam* (“as”) should be read, as in our manuscript.] as Mother of God and bride of the Holy Spirit, and most loving daughter of God the Father. You sit at the right hand of the eternal King, as a most illustrious queen, crowned with glory and honor, clothed in a golden garment adorned with wondrous variety, and most excellently praised by the chorus and harmony of all angels and saints.

Therefore, for both—the death-pang of your Son and the ineffable glory with which you now rejoice in heaven—I desire in some way to soothe you with these words:

> Hail, celibate Virgin,  
> Compared with the lily,  
> Slain by the sword of the cross,  
> [Note: [Col. 0291D] Alva’s *crucifixaque* (“and crucified”) is improper and does not fit the meter. Our manuscript has the reading printed here.] And pierced by the sword.  
>
> But when your Son has risen,  
> May you be gladdened,  
> And sorrow driven away,  
> Heaped up with joy.  
>
> Now exalted in heaven,  
> You dwell upon the throne,  
> Adorned becomingly  
> With a radiant mantle,  
> Crowned with bright stars,  
> Reverently contemplated  
> In the noble company  
> Of virgins,  
> And with the rejoicing of all  
> Praised forever.  
>
> Amen.

Rightly, therefore, most merciful Lady, you are to be praised and glorified by all, since you confer grace upon everyone and increase punishment for no one. You bestow peace upon earth, grace upon heaven, salvation upon the lost, and life upon the dead; you govern prosperity, repel adversity, extinguish vices, kindle virtues, make bodies chaste and hearts pure; you give peace to the limbs, tranquil faith to minds, the order of life to peoples, and discipline to conduct.

For you, Lady, are admirable in your singular virginity, lovable in your life-giving fruitfulness, and venerable in your incomparable holiness. You displayed to the world its visible Savior; you gave birth to the world’s restorer; you offered to the world its Lord and Creator. You are proclaimed by divine and angelic praises, remaining holy in mind and body, exalted by many privileges of gifts, dwelling with the senators of heaven within the court of paradise, formed under the discipline and instruction of the Holy Spirit in the fullness of divinity, overshadowed by the power of the Most High, and made fruitful and pregnant by the saving dew of the Holy Spirit.

You are the exemplar of continence and chastity; you are the form of perfect integrity. [Note: [Col. 0291D] Alva has *tu ne praecellis* (“you do not surpass”); we excluded *ne* (“not”) in accordance with our manuscript.] You surpass all, excelling everyone. You are a holy virgin, a sober virgin, a devout virgin, singular in integrity, outstanding in integrity. You conceived without loss of modesty and gave birth without pain. You gave birth to the life and light of human beings. You, a virgin, conceived God from the Holy Spirit and gave birth to him undefiled. You, beautiful Virgin, conceived in the chaste womb of chastity one more beautiful in form than the sons of men and more beautiful than the daughters of men, and you offered him to us.

### Prayer

[Col. 0291D] Since, therefore, you are the most merciful, sweetest, and most powerful Mother of God, have mercy on me in the day of my tribulation and need. Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied and have hated and persecuted me with wicked hatred; they have seized my soul [Note: [Col. 0291D] Our manuscript has *corripuerunt* (“they seized”); Alva has *corrumpunt* (“they corrupt”)], wounded it, violated it, and trampled it beneath their feet.

Reconcile me, my Lady, to my Creator, whom you clothed in your holy flesh. Restore me to my God, whom you nourished with virginal milk, so that [Note: [Col. 0291D] Alva: “the holy merits of the birth,” etc.] through your holy merits, visited by his grace, raised up by his mercy, illumined by his light, and strengthened by his power, I may be able to despise my enemies, accomplish virtuous works, cling perfectly to my Creator, and sing and chant perpetual praises to him and to you forever. Amen.

## Chapter V. The lily, a white flower, is placed in the fourth place of the Virgin’s crown

Maria, treasure and garden of blessing, pillar and foundation of truth, splendor and radiance of grace, vein and pardon of indulgence, empress and teacher of glory, foundation of the Church, fountain of wisdom, court of modesty, hope of salvation and pardon, full of virtue and grace, seat of peace, court of blessedness, land of blessing, parent of truth, minister of salvation, lover of the humble, honor of the continent, light of sinners, [Note: [Col. 0292D] Our manuscript has “unction of penitents.”] strength of penitents, way of the wandering, teacher of the perfect, joy of angels and human beings:

For the glory and beauty of your crown, in its fourth place I set the Lily, a pleasing and beautiful flower. The lily has whiteness in its color, sweetness in its fragrance, gentleness on its surface, and beauty in its appearance; these qualities suit you, and therefore it rightly ought to be placed in your crown.

In the whiteness [Note: [Col. 0292D] “Of the Son” was read in both manuscripts, certainly incorrectly.] of the Lily, virginity is signified. For you were a Virgin pure in mind and made chaste in body; and just as you possessed virginity in body, so you possessed purity and cleanliness in conscience. You were a virgin in childbirth and remained inviolate after childbirth.

[Note: [Col. 0292D] Our manuscript reads *decorata* (“adorned”).] Therefore, beautiful in your flesh through the whiteness of virginity and in your soul through the splendor of humility and purity, you pleased the Son of God through the twofold adornment of holiness and virtue. You, Lady, are unique, for no other pleased God as you did, nor built so beautiful a palace for him. Therefore, just as no one is good in comparison with God, so in comparison with you no one is found perfect, although some may be proved exceptional.

But what smells so sweet to the soul as your name, sprinkled abroad? Concerning this name someone has said:

> Mary’s name is gold [F., golden],  
> Fragrant and aromatic,  
> Like heavenly perfume:  
>
> Bright with light like the sun,  
> Giving life to the dead,  
> Honey-sweet to monks,  
> Holy and leading upward,  
> Divine and ecstatic.

You are also a very gentle and mild Lady. Holy Scripture proclaims you a teacher of gentleness, a standard of kindness, a rule of modesty, and a model of meekness. You are also an exceedingly beautiful girl, a most beautiful virgin, and unknown to man (Genesis 24:16). No woman is like you in appearance, beauty, or the meaning of her words. Because you were very beautiful in the adornment of virginal chastity, in the incredible beauty of complete holiness, and in the precious array of all virtues, you were pleasing, exceedingly lovable, and gracious in the eyes of the supreme King.

You also possessed beauty in your eyes because of the simplicity dwelling there, elegance on your lips because of the eloquence flowing from them, beauty in your hands because of the generosity overflowing from them, and loveliness in your ears because of the pity that inclined them. [Col. 0292D] Who is sufficient to recount your virtues or explain your wonders?

You are higher than heaven and deeper than the abyss. You carried in your immaculate womb God, whom the world cannot contain. You restored the losses of the first mother; you discovered redemption for lost humanity [Note: [Col. 0292D] Our manuscript has *adduxisti* (“you brought”);] and offered the world a unique exchange. You surpass every creature in holiness and dignity. You join heavenly and earthly things in one covenant [Note: [Col. 0292D] Alva: “and earthly things with a covenant.”], raise us to heavenly and higher things, confirm the pact, and dissolve the bonds of death.

You, royal Virgin adorned with the gems of virtues, shining with the twofold beauty of mind and body, known in the heavens for your appearance and beauty, drew the gaze of the heavenly citizens toward you, so that you inclined the King’s mind toward desire for you [Note: [Col. 0293D] Alva: “that he might incline … and bring out …”] and brought the heavenly messenger to you from above.

You conceived, and without sin; you were pregnant, but not burdened; you gave birth, but were not corrupted; giving birth to God and conceiving from God; knowing no man and bringing forth a Son; a chaste mother in childbirth, an untouched mother, the mother of him whose Father is God. The Son of paternal charity is the crown of your chastity; the wisdom of the paternal heart is the fruit of your virginal womb. You are the flower bringing forth a flower, the virgin bringing forth a virgin bridegroom, the crown of virgins.

You were loved by the Lord above salvation and every beauty. Without the touch of shame you were found to be the mother of the Savior. You alone, a Virgin, were worthy to bear the Lord of all and to nurse the King of angels. You illumine the world with the radiance of virtues and brighten hearts with the light of justice, because you always shine with the splendor of grace and are stained by no filth of guilt.

I therefore greet you, queen [Col. 0293B] of virgins, rose of spring, lily of the valley; by greeting you I wish to end this chapter.

## Prayer

Hail, full of heavenly grace, full of God, and full of glory. Lilies of virgins surround you; rewards of virtues accompany you. Virgin of God, Virgin in childbirth, overshadowed by heavenly power.

You are that light-bearing cloud [Note: [Col. 0293D] “Which you illumine” is absent from Alva’s edition.] which illumines heaven and the stars; whitened ivory tower, crimson-colored rose. So that the gall-filled legion may be overthrown, the sword has been entrusted to you.

Since you are the salvation and honor of humanity, Mother of God, crown of virgins, may boundless honor rightly be paid to you after the Lord.

## Chapter VI. The placement of the precious Chalcedony stone in the crown of the Virgin Mary

Virgin and wondrous Lady, through whom Tartarus has been broken, heavenly things preserved, lost things restored, and the elements renewed: shining before all in singular beauty, radiant and flashing with singular loveliness, to the honor and glory of your most holy head, in the fifth place of your illustrious crown I set the precious stone Chalcedony, outstanding in power.

Chalcedony, which is dark indoors but glows beneath the open sky, shines in your diadem, for your virtues and miracles are no longer hidden in a corner but spread throughout the whole world. Everywhere your name is proclaimed, your fruit is blessed, your womb is exalted, [Note: [Col. 0294D] Alva: “your words.”] and your breasts are venerated. The sound of your virtues has gone out into all the earth, and the voice of your miracles has been heard to the ends of the world (Psalm 18:5).

Throughout the world you illumine souls, revive bodies, raise the dead, heal the sick, restore the poor, support the weak, strengthen what is broken, restore what is lost, and preserve what has been gathered. You restore sight to the blind, walking to the lame, and hearing to the deaf; eloquence is given to the mute, knowledge to the ignorant, medicine to the sick. Your grace is poured into all, your pity comes to the aid of all, and your mercy supports everyone.

O blessed and supremely blessed Virgin, bearing the blessed fruit through whom all things—heaven, earth, and seas—are blessed! O beautiful to behold, lovable to contemplate, delightful to love! The sun and moon marvel at your beauty; hearts are illumined by your splendor; angelic powers serve you [F., “serve whom”]; your riches never fail, your riches never diminish. You are pleasing to God, angels, and human beings: to God through humility, to angels through virginity, to human beings through fruitfulness.

> You are the chamber guarding perfumes,  
> The court of heavenly mysteries,  
> Bright star of sailors,  
> Straight path of those who do not wander,  
> Praise of the singing saints,  
> True salvation of the sick.  
>
> Ark of wisdom,  
> Tabernacle of glory,  
> Rule of justice,  
> Power of temperance,  
> Rose of modesty.  
>
> Fragrant nard,  
> Almond tree of gentleness,  
> Evergreen laurel of chastity,  
> Fruit-bearing olive.  
>
> Blooming garden when the south wind blows,  
> Closed gate behind and before,  
> Way of truth along the way.  
>
> Earth poured over with heaven’s dew,  
> Gideon’s fleece drenched,  
> Rain of divinity.  
>
> Appease, Mary, Star of the Sea,  
> Lest the storm engulf us  
> And the tempest engulf everything.

O most radiant queen, fullest of every good! Through you glory is rendered back to God, joy to the angels, salvation to sinners, comfort to the despairing, health to the sick, brightness to the blind, joy to the sorrowful, consolation to the mourners, steadfastness to fighters, glory to the just, and an unfading crown.

You are care healing the sick, joy comforting the sorrowful, health gladdening those in pain:

> You are the humble valley,  
> Uncultivated earth,  
> Which brought forth fruit:  
> Flower of the valley fields,  
> Singular lily.  
> Christ came forth from you.  
>
> You are the heavenly paradise,  
> And uncut Lebanon,  
> Exhaling sweetness,  
> You who possess the beauty  
> Of whiteness and loveliness,  
> Of sweetness and fragrance.

You are the mother of the holy deity [Note: [Col. 0294D] Our manuscript has “of the holy deity”], radiant with brilliance and illumining the earth with the clarity of heavenly light. You, light of purity and holiness, prepared for God the most immaculate dwelling. On the heavenly throne, above the ranks of angels, you shine with perpetual brightness. Like a star before Lucanum, you drench us with morning dew.

Shining more brilliantly in holiness than the lights in the firmament of heaven, inflamed with charity, you contemplate the deifying light nearer than all the angels. Radiating with the pure light of wisdom and virtue, you drove away the fearful darkness of the ages with the splendor of virtues.

You are the mother of salvation, who alone can bring medicine to the despairing; from whose virginal womb God came forth for the salvation of his people. Mother of salvation, through whom conquered death fell and the salvation of humanity, once despaired of, rose again. Mother of salvation, who raises up the ruins of the fallen mind and restrains [F., extinguishes] the burning illness of seething [Col. 0294D] sins.

## Prayer

Have mercy, therefore—so powerful, so gracious, so sweet, so devout, so beautiful, and so lovely—on this sinful servant. Wash and cleanse me from sins and vices; irradiate my breast with your light, inflame my soul with your love, obtain for me from your Son peace and pardon, and on the day of judgment a glorified resurrection. Amen.

## Chapter VII. The placement of the brilliant luminary Arcturus in the Virgin’s crown

Most serene queen, undefiled Mother of God, pure Virgin, holy Virgin, immaculate Virgin, whose virginity we praise, whose humility we marvel at, but whose mercy and pity we invoke more dearly—for it tastes sweeter to the wretched.

Your nard and perfumes are the gifts of the Holy Spirit dwelling in you, illuminating you and inflaming you with his love. Your fruit is eternal; its fragrance fills the world, its taste satisfies the faithful [Note: [Col. 0295D] Alva: “heals”], and its splendor surpasses the sun.

Since, therefore, you have brought forth for us so precious a fruit from the fruitful vine, I set Arcturus in the sixth place of your crown, to add something to the honor and glory of your magnificence: a bright and shining luminary adorned with seven stars, in the form of a wagon.

In this, Lady, you resemble and in a manner correspond to it. You were luminous in virginity, bright in faith and holiness, and most resplendent in fruitfulness. You were adorned with seven stars when you were adorned with the seven virtues. You were [Note: [Col. 0295D] “Made firm,” the same.] made firm through faith, inflamed with love through charity, raised upward through hope, sober and modest through temperance, strengthened through fortitude, supremely just through justice, and most eloquent through prudence.

You were the chariot of God, carrying almighty God in your holy soul and bearing the Lord Jesus Christ in your holy womb. You are also the chariot of Israel, kindly bearing our sins, obtaining pardon and peace for us, and providing your guidance on the road to paradise.

My Lady, solace of my heart, sweetness of my soul, refreshment of my spirit: mercifully bear my vices and sins, my harsh and iron-like ways. Through your merits may peace and pardon be granted to me; through you may the way to paradise be shown to me, and the heavenly doors and gate be opened.

Therefore, my illustrious Lady, [Note: [Col. 0295D] Alva printed: “Tell me what I should present to you,” etc.] tell me what beautiful and pleasing thing I may offer you; show me what lovable and joyful thing I may present and give you; reveal what delightful and beautiful thing I may give you. [Note: [Col. 0295D] We corrected *pota* (“give to drink”) from our manuscript; Alva printed *nuti*, though perhaps *nutri* (“nourish”) was intended.]

Give this foul sinner drink from the abundance of your fullness of purity; feed this loathsome worm from the wealth of your sweetness; rescue me from the hand of hostile power; confound all my adversaries. As smoke [Note: [Col. 0295D] Alva: “may they fail.”] disappears, so may all my enemies perish; may your power, Lady, crush them; may hell swallow them alive.

[Note: [Col. 0295D] We print this sentence according to our manuscript. In Alva’s edition the words “open now the door of your light” [Col. 0296D] occur immediately before “and from your fountain,” in a disordered sequence.]

Open now, O Davidic key, the honey-sweet inward parts of your heart; open now the door of your light, so that I may enter, see, and taste the sweetness of your breasts, and so that my thirsty soul may be made drunk from your sweetest fountain. Through this wondrous refreshment may I learn to love you with all the affection of my heart and all the effort of my mind—fervently and prudently, sincerely and joyfully, humbly and devoutly.

Give me a voice of praise, so that I may know how worthily to recount your wonders. Blessed be your flowering virginity; blessed be your virginal fruitfulness; blessed be your gracious humility; blessed be your compassionate pity; blessed be your holiness, by which you become more excellent than all; blessed be your dignity, more precious than all. [Note: [Col. 0296D] Alva repeats *sanctitas* (“holiness”); our manuscript has *dignitas* (“dignity”).]

For the Holy Spirit, with his honey-sweet dew, made your virginal womb fruitful and overshadowed your most holy body with a divine covering [Col. 0295D]. Your blessed soul, which is the noble dining chamber of the Holy Trinity, is most nobly marked out: it is adorned with the gold of faith, the silver of wisdom, precious stones, the fleece [F., wool] of holiness, roses of modesty, lilies of chastity, and violets of virginity. It is illumined by the sun of justice, radiated by the moon of purity and the stars of innocence, adorned with every treasure [Col. 0296A] of grace, and ennobled with every sacred spiritual gift.

## Prayer

O Virgin Lady, heaped up and filled with so many and such great goods! Be gracious to us in our needs, sweet in tribulations, devout in difficulties, ready and suited to help in dangers. You are also refreshment for the troubled, you offer consolation to the sorrowful, and you soothe the tears of those who weep.

The burden of crimes presses upon us; the waters of desires flow down; the waves of pleasures surge. But O you who have pity on the wretched, console us with your consolations. And lest [Note: [Col. 0296D] Better than Alva: *induamur* (“we be clothed”).] we be enveloped in perpetual darkness, lest we be assigned to eternal punishments, help us in the painful hour of fearful death; lead us to the joy of the holy resurrection and to the joy of perpetual brightness. Amen.

## Chapter VIII. The precious sapphire stone is placed in the Virgin’s crown

[Col. 0296B]

Noble banqueting chamber of the Holy Trinity, holy reclining-place of the Father’s Word, lovely girl, beautiful virgin, radiant and serene queen, devout, sweet, full of grace—to you God granted that, first among women [Note: Alva, “first”], you should offer God the gift of virginity. Therefore you rightly deserved to enjoy an angelic appearance and conduct [F., “speech”], since you strove to imitate the angelic life. For in you, while the heavens distill their dew, the whole fullness of divinity pours itself forth; in you the fullness of grace, the indwelling of God, and heavenly blessing were offered and bestowed.

Therefore, since so many marks of wonder are so excellently proclaimed in you, I, a sinner wishing still to enlarge your glory, have resolved to place in the seventh position of your crown the most precious stone, the sapphire. The sapphire resembles a serene sky; when struck by the sun’s ray, it emits a fiery brilliance. Its power is to purify the body, benefit the eyes, and counteract poisons. And this stone rightly suits the adornment of your head. [Col. 0296C] You, Lady, were always radiant and serene, sincere, most pure, and lovely. For you are always wholly beautiful, wholly fair, wholly immaculate, and wholly comely. No stain darkens you; no filth defiles you. You are illumined by every grace and adorned with every virtue. In your appearance you are more beautiful and comelier than the sun, and you shine with exceptional beauty above the entire arrangement of the stars.

But when that supreme Majesty, whose beloved bride and cherished daughter you are, reflects its gracious and lovely ray upon your face, then my hope is increased by greater beauty, your wisdom shines with more abundant light [Note: Our manuscript reads “is radiated”], your charity becomes wholly burning with love of God, and all your virtues are suffused with greater holiness. You also, Lady, purify minds and bodies, illumine the eyes of mind and body, and remove and uproot the poisons of sins. [Note: Alva printed, from his own corrupt text, “you nourish the poisons of animals.”]

Since, then, Lady, you are the salvation of the human race, the hope and solace of the poor, come to the aid of us wretched little servants. For hostile wars press upon us; enemies spread their nets [Note: “Above, they extend nets,” Alva]; the flesh suggests softness, the devil quarrels and disputes, the world riches and honors, and every kind of curiosity. O Queen of mercy, come to our aid in the time of distress; bring us the help of your grace. And lest we fall amid such dangers, remain with us, Lady, because evening is coming on. You are the fountain of salvation and of all grace, the way of peace and the harbor of forgiveness; hear the laments [Col. 0297A] of your household. Many dangers surround us; severe illness consumes the body; a most bitter temptation burns the breast; the rain of devotion is restrained; fervor in prayer is not found; the eye of reason is darkened. [Note: Alva reads “the eyes of reason.”]

## Prayer

O refuge of the poor! O refreshment of the wretched! In you all eyes hope, that we may be freed from such deadly evils, since it is yours to save whomever you wish. Remain with us, because evening is coming on; free us from darkness and the shadow of death, and lead us to the glory of everlasting immortality. Amen.

## Chapter IX. The aromatic crocus flower in the Virgin’s crown

If I could proclaim your praises, most holy Virgin, in the tongues of all nations and with all the melodies of the angels, I would still be wholly unable to do so adequately; for in my praises no fitting instrument is found, and the talent of every subtle intellect is dull. For the Holy Spirit, the fountain and source of every good, has so heaped upon you his own insignia of virtues and the gifts of graces [Note: Alva, in place of “his own,” which is found in our manuscript, printed “above,” as shortly before] that neither the honor you possess in the world, nor the glory you possess in heaven, nor the crown you possess as a reward could be expressed by an angelic spirit or a human intellect.

Since, then, all should praise you greatly, most serene Virgin, I, a sinner, for your honor and glory, desire in the eighth position of your renowned crown to place the aromatic crocus flower, highly suitable for you. The crocus is golden in color, pleasing in fragrance [Note: Alva corruptly printed from his own text: “golden in color, something that pleases”], marvelous in virtue, and exceedingly joy-giving.

For you are a golden virgin, adorned with every holiness. Your holiness is signified by gold; just as gold surpasses all metals in nobility and value, so the dignity of your holiness surpasses the merits of all the saints and the prerogatives of all the angels. Therefore you hold the highest place above all in heaven. Thus, just as in the whole world there is no place more worthy than the temple of your virginal womb in which you received the Son of God, so in heaven there is no place more worthy than that royal throne on which the Son of God exalted you above all the saints.

You are also more fragrant than the crocus, because before God and human beings you breathe fragrance and emit perfume. Hence your fragrance is like the scent of a full field that the Lord has blessed (Genesis 27:27). Your holy womb is a full field that produced the blessed harvest by which angels and human beings are sustained. Yet the fragrance proceeding from your humility greatly delights God; the fragrance proceeding from your virginity greatly delights the angels; the fragrance proceeding from your piety greatly refreshes human beings; and the fragrance proceeding from your holiness greatly terrifies demons.

You were and are also marvelous in virtue. For the virtue proceeding from you clarifies sight, moderates taste, restores hearing, strengthens the heart, and illumines the intellect. Your grace, Lady, produces joy in us in many ways: for you, most devout Virgin, frequently console the sorrowful, soften what is harsh, bring joy to what is painful, strengthen the weak, sustain the feeble, give life to the dead, heal the sick, and free them.

For all these things, Lady, let us rejoice in your glory and honor; let us exult in your praises; let us take delight in your proclamations; let us rejoice together in your crowns and rewards. Therefore, concerning the sweetness and jubilation poured from you into a loving heart [Note: Alva, “into an agreeing mind”], someone says:

> Oil poured out,  
> ointment emptied,  
> jubilation of hearts:  
> the holy and glorious name of Mary.

But let the alabaster jar be broken. Descend, Lady, into my garden; kindle there a burning love; let fall the ointment of your beauty; sprinkle the fragrance of your spices.

[Col. 0298A]

## Prayer

Let Mary be in our memory; let Mary’s sweetness and grace be explored; let Mary’s benefits and tireless charity be recalled. And deign graciously to receive these verses, Lady, which I now offer to you, commending them for the honor of your glory.

> Hail, river of mercy,  
> river of peace and river of grace,  
> dew of the valleys,  
> flower of modesty,  
> Mother of God  
> and mother of forgiveness.
>
> Hail, true salvation of the faithful,  
> throne and seat of Majesty,  
> temple of Christ,  
> house and banqueting chamber,  
> way of life, lily of modesty.
>
> Hail, flower of lovely beauty,  
> humble servant-bride of Christ,  
> wholly beautiful and venerable,  
> to whom no one was ever like.
>
> We proclaim you venerable,  
> holy in mind and simple in heart,  
> pure in the flesh,  
> gentle and peaceable,  
> pleasing to God,  
> beloved of God.
>
> Those who taste you still hunger;  
> they thirst for your holy sweetness.  
> They ardently desire to love you;  
> they desire to praise you, but cannot suffice.
>
> Holy Mother of God and of humanity, praise and ornament of the human race, surpassing the saints in holiness and shining more brightly than the others in splendor—who can worthily exalt you? Who can offer you worthy praises? [Note: Alva, “deserves them.”]

Since you were worthy to bear God and to nurse him at your sacred breast, our salvation is in your hand, Lady. May your mercy look upon us so greatly that we may serve God, the eternal King, without fear, [Col. 0298C] and you, his blessed Mother. O Queen of glory, who live and reign with God upon the throne of supreme Majesty, through infinite ages of ages. Amen.

## Chapter X. The placing of the precious agate stone in the crown of the Virgin Mary

You sit upon the heavenly throne, most radiant Queen, crowned with glory and honor, adorned with the jewels of virtues, exceedingly joyful, exceedingly fair, exceedingly beautiful: beautiful in virginity, more beautiful in humility, most beautiful in the conception of the Son of God; beautiful in the praise of reputation, more beautiful in the uprightness of conduct, most beautiful in the glory of the divine vision.

Beautiful, because you possessed neither stain nor wrinkle, nor any defilement of flesh or spirit, but were wholly pure like refined gold, wholly brilliant, wholly white, wholly glowing, wholly spotless. From your heart and conduct every stain of sin was far removed; the grace and gift of all holiness clung firmly to you.

So beautiful, Lady, and so comely and fair, graciously receive the agate stone, which, to enlarge your adornment, I have decided to place in the ninth position of your crown. Agate makes a person gracious among the other virtues; it befits you, Lady, to have it in the adornment of your head, because you work this in us more effectively.

We are dark in sins, muddy in desires, and shadowed by vices; therefore we are hateful and detestable to God, like sons of gehenna. For many are swollen with pride, blackened by avarice, bloodstained by anger, foul through lust, muddied by gluttony, livid through envy, and drowsy through sloth.

But when [Note: Alva, “For indeed when”] it pleased him who set you apart from your mother’s womb to come to the aid of the wretched, so that your compassion might be stirred for us, then, with your hand acting as midwife, we are brought out from dark works and introduced into virtuous ones. Vices are detested; fasts are embraced. Desires are extinguished; virtues come back to life. You open your hand and fill every living thing with blessing (Psalm 145:4, 16). When the seed of your grace is scattered in us, the proud become humble, the avaricious compassionate, the gluttonous temperate, the lustful chaste, the angry charitable, and the lazy industrious. Thus those who formerly displeased God like sons of darkness now, through you, become pleasing, like sons of light and coheirs with Christ of the heavenly kingdom.

Therefore glory in the highest to God, who has provided us with so useful and necessary an agent, whose care and office it is to empty Tartarus, illumine the world, irradiate heaven, fill paradise, crush the devil, snatch prey from his mouth, and gather sinners through repentance into the inheritance, like a most loving mother.

O Mary, then, full of grace, radiant virgin, wholly golden, pure and undefiled, consecrated as Christ’s dwelling, a vessel made beautiful and glorious through adornment, pleasing and acceptable in the eyes of the supreme King, sanctified by the blessing of the Holy Spirit! O virginal girl, consecrated by the Holy Spirit, protected and guarded by the holy angels, surrounded and comforted by archangels and angels, and adorned with many graces and virtues!

Turn toward me, Lady, your tender and sweet eye, merciful and gracious, shining and luminous. Visit me in my sickness; tend me in my illness; heal me in my weakness; console me, sorrowful and sighing. Give me a devout heart and an illumined intellect, so that I may be able to know the generosity of your goodness and mercy, the purity of your virginal flesh, the depth of your intellect and wisdom, and the holiness of your body and soul.

Look upon me, supreme Empress, from the height of your most excellent majesty, and illumine the darkness of my heart with the splendors of your grace; restore in me an ever-watchful mind; set me aflame with your love.

[Col. 0299C]

## Prayer

I pray that your virginity may make me chaste; your fruitfulness may adorn me with virtues; your humility may make me humble [Note: Our manuscript reads “gentle”]; your piety may make me devout and sweet; your holiness may make me contrite and sighing; your clemency may make me worthy of eternal glory; and, as long as I live, may it make me devoted to your praises and songs.

For the body is worn down by harsh torments, the spirit is broken by temptations, and inward sweetness is withdrawn from us. O sacred Queen of virgins, give solace, bring remedy, behold the tears of those who cry out to you. And lest we fall into vices, lest we become like beasts, remain with us, Lady, because evening is coming on.

Therefore, venerable and undefiled Virgin, crowned in heaven through your wondrous childbirth, make this tearful soul, burdened with sorrows, gentle and humble and cleansed of filth, so that through a peaceful death it may go, contrite and devout, to noble, flourishing, and radiant life, far removed from evils. Amen.

## Chapter XI. The splendid Morning Star in the Virgin’s crown

To praise, bless, and proclaim you, most holy Mother of Christ, we are admonished by the Scriptures, stimulated by examples, urged on by benefits, inflamed by inward inspirations, and moved by manifest miracles. You gave birth to God for humanity; you obtained peace for the world; you overcame and conquered the devil; you restored the human race; and through you all good things in heaven and on earth have been accomplished.

You are the most noble and holy throne of the Holy Trinity; the beautiful and virginal bridal chamber of the incarnate Word of the Father; the most precious stone in the crown of the eternal Emperor; the dearest daughter of the supreme Father; the most loving bride of the Holy Spirit; the Lady and Queen of angels and human beings.

You are a wondrous choir, full of wisdom, illumined by splendor, endowed with the eyes of knowledge, bright with every grace, perfect in beauty. In the midst of the burning stones—that is, the angels and archangels—you shone with wondrous glory, surpassing in holiness all the cedars and all who are in the paradise of God.

You are a Seraph with six wings, bearing the stigmata of Jesus Christ [Note: Alva, “the stigma”], inflamed with love of the Creator, suspended by divine visions, and rapt in contemplation of the most excellent Majesty.

Therefore, although unworthy, wishing to honor so illustrious a Lady, in accordance with the intention already stated, I place in the tenth position of your precious crown the Star of the Sea, which directs sailors and navigators [Note: Our manuscript reads “rowers”]. For the Star of the Sea directs navigators, consoles and raises them, and brings them to the desired harbor.

You, Lady, are that Star of the Sea, who amid the waves of temptations, amid the dangers of worldly affairs, [Col. 0300B] amid the pains of illnesses, rule and guide us, grant help and counsel, pour joy into us, and lead our souls to harbor. A certain servant and devoted praiser of yours [Note: Saint Bernard, *Homily 2 on “Missus est,” near the end] admonishes us in his little works to implore the patronage of this Star with attentive hearts, saying:

## Prayer

> In dangers and doubtful matters, look to the Star, invoke Mary. Let her not depart from your heart; let her not depart from your mouth. Following her, you do not go astray; thinking of her, you do not err; asking her, you do not despair; while she holds you, you do not fear; while she protects you, you do not fall; while she guides you, you do not grow weary; with her as guide, you reach the heavenly realms.
>
> May this happen to us through your holy patronage and glorious merits, with the assent of your blessed Son, with whom you live and reign throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

## Chapter XII. Here the precious jasper stone is placed in the crown of our Lady

[Col. 0300C]

Blessed are you, Lady and Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, Mother of mercies and Lady of all consolation, who console us in all our tribulation. And blessed be the name of your glory, holy [Note: “and praiseworthy” is absent from Alva’s edition], praiseworthy, and exalted above all forever.

O gate of paradise! O minister of the grace of the Holy Spirit! O teacher of all theoretical and divine knowledge! Teacher of Christ’s humility and poverty!

You are brighter than the patriarchs in faith and patience; keener than the prophets in understanding and wisdom; richer than the apostles in perfection of holiness; you surpass the martyrs in enduring sufferings, the confessors in practicing virtuous deeds, and virgins in purity of chastity. You surpass angels and archangels in administering graces; dominations in overthrowing vices and desires; principalities and powers in restraining hostile power; thrones in the tranquility of peace; cherubim in the splendor of wisdom; seraphim in the ardor of charity.

Since, then, you are exceedingly wondrous, Lady, because you surpass all others in every knowledge, every grace, holiness, and virtue, and no one is like you, I, a sinner wishing to obtain grace with you, place in the eleventh position of your noble crown the jasper, a precious stone.

Jasper is a virtuous and precious stone, beautiful in its variety of colors [Note: Alva, “pleasing in appearance”], conspicuous for its greenness, and especially effective for restraining blood. It is well suited to adorn your holy head, Lady. For you were adorned with a variety of virtues, ornamented with the green of virginity and faith, and given to us by God as a salutary and effective medicine for restraining blood—that is, the desires and pleasures of the flesh.

Although you were impregnated, you were nevertheless made fruitful by the Holy Spirit and deified through childbirth. Although vigorous through strength, virtuous through uprightness, loving through charity, luminous through wisdom, ingenious through intelligence, tender-hearted through piety, humble in prosperity, strong in adversity, and exalted in holiness, the greenness of virginity nevertheless always revived in your body, and the beauty of faith always revived in your sacred mind.

You also restrain and dry up the blood of sinners, check and cool the flow of the flesh, and clarify and heal whatever is stained in us.

## Prayer

Therefore, most pure girl, lover of virginity, extinguish in my body the itch and filth of lust, and by life-giving dew [Note: Our manuscript reads “salutary”] create in me the purity of flowering chastity.

In every prayer, meditation, reading, and action, may my mind feel the sweetness of your presence and the angelic justification that consoles, guides, and protects me. Anoint my heart with the most precious ointment of your sweetness, so that I may be able to feel the sweetness of your love, the delight of your charity, and the soothing pleasure and joy of friendship.

But I, wretched and blind, constantly wandering through outward things, depart from your holy love and seek wicked consolations in carnal pleasures. Hence I do not delight in your charity and sweetness, because I am entangled in transient and perishable things in thought, affection, and speech.

But you, Lady, loving heavenly things, dwell in inaccessible light. You are in heaven, and I am on earth. You love incorruptible and eternal goods; I love things fleeting and perishable, in which there is nothing but vanity, misery, and affliction of spirit.

What more need I add? You are devout, holy, just, and merciful; I am wicked, impious, unjust, and without mercy. You are light; I am blind. You are life; I am dead. You are joy; I am sorrow.

Behold, I cry out to you: Mother of God the Savior, give me life; Mother of the Redeemer, redeem me; Mother of the Savior, save me. And lest I be endangered, glorious Lady, by deadly pleasures in these temporal things [Note: Alva, “by deadly pleasures in these temporal things”], I beg you to hold my heart, rule my mind, direct my intellect, and lift up my spirit, so that through the power of your love I may cling perfectly to you [Note: “to you” is absent in Alva’s edition] and sleep and rest in the abundance of your sweetness and grace.

## Chapter XIII. The placing of the vernal rose in the Virgin’s crown

Hierarchical Queen, existing as a seraphic throne in which the majesty and glory, power and authority, honor and magnificence of the entire Holy Trinity reside and shine forth—whom angels and archangels, cherubim and seraphim, all the hosts of heavenly citizens and phalanxes of the spirits above praise—because what in them had been ruined and broken has through you, Lady, been more splendidly built and restored.

Therefore, not forgetful or ungrateful for the benefits received through you, they sing hymnic praises in your glorification with festive voices, with every harmony and honor, saying:

> Who is she who comes forth like the rising dawn, beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as an army arranged for battle? (Song 6:9)

For when you were born, you rose like a gleaming dawn. Your birth indeed took the place of dawn, in which the day of grace began and the night of unbelief and ignorance came to an end [F., “made an end”]. You possessed the beauty of the full moon when you became full of grace in the conception of the incarnate Word.

When you give birth to the sun of righteousness, you are compared to the sun in a fitting likeness. For just as the sun’s body is neither corrupted nor diminished by a ray issuing forth, so your giving birth did not violate the emergence of the sacred offspring. To you, Mother of mercy, belongs the sun’s election, for you display the eternal rays of splendor to all.

You appeared terrible as an army arranged for battle when, with the heavens rejoicing, the angels obeying, the saints exulting, and the banners of virtues flashing, you appeared terrible to the demons.

O wondrous Lady, therefore, marked by solar brightness and adorned with lunar beauty, graciously receive the vernal rose that I offer you, so that it may be placed in the twelfth position of your noble crown.

The rose is called, by excellence, the flower of flowers. It is exceedingly pleasing and welcome in appearance; in fragrance it is wonderfully delightful; it is beneficial and useful in medicine. All these qualities suit you perfectly, gracious Virgin.

But you, Lady, are not the rose of the world, which withers and fades immediately after its arising; you are the rose of paradise, carried in the hand of the King of heaven. You are the flower of virginal flowers and the queen of all Christ’s maidens. For from you they received the form of integrity and, as from an outstanding teacher, the instruction of perfect chastity. Therefore you sit triumphing above all upon the throne of imperial dignity.

You too, Lady, are beautiful in faith, beautiful before God in humility, beautiful before the angels in virginity, and beautiful before human beings in mercy and piety. The fragrance of your piety is perceived in heaven; the perfume of your mercy is perceived in the world [Note: Alva, “is worshiped”]; the sweetness of your compassion is sprinkled throughout hell.

The fragrance of your humility made the Son of the supreme King descend from the heavenly throne and compelled him to recline in the dwelling of your virginal womb. Concerning that dwelling, a certain devout poet wrote:

> The sun is brighter than the moon,  
> and the moon than the stars;  
> so Mary is more worthy  
> than all creatures.
>
> Hail, Mother of piety  
> and of the entire Trinity,  
> noble sanctuary,  
> preparing for the incarnate Word  
> a special lodging  
> for Majesty.

Your medicine also comes to the aid of illness, helps in adversity, refreshes in labor, consoles in sorrow; in persecution it provides assistance [Note: Alva, “providing”; and shortly below, for “removes,” he printed “illumines,” whereas we print the reading of our manuscript], in tribulation consolation; it heals bodily diseases and removes the vices of the heart. Hence someone says: “For every danger the Virgin’s piety comes to our aid, and she is powerful to help.”

## Prayer

Since, then, so many and such great are the prerogatives of your merits, O beautiful light, illumine my sight so that it may contemplate your beauty; heal my taste so that it may savor your sweetness; renew my sense of smell so that it may perceive your fragrance. Illumine and inflame all my inward parts with your holy wisdom and your flame-emitting charity [Note: Alva, “flaming matter”], so that I may know how wisely to think about you, fervently to love you, devoutly to honor you, profoundly to understand you, wisely to investigate you, sweetly to meditate upon you, and tenderly to cling to you.

Stand by me, Lady, as I devoutly beseech you, sweetly meditate upon you, read of you, meditate on you, speak about you, and anxiously sigh toward you. May your fragrance refresh me, your memory strengthen me, your sweetness restore me, your grace nourish me, your piety sweeten me, your presence console me, and your guidance accompany me, leading me along your paths to the light in which you dwell. Amen.

## Chapter XIV. The placing of the precious carbuncle stone in the Virgin’s crown

[Col. 0303A]

Royal branch [F., “virgin”], adorned with the jewels of virtues, arranged with the necklaces of graces, clothed in the garment of righteousness, known in the heavenly realms for your appearance and beauty—your goodness so inclined the King’s spirit toward desire for you that he sent his messenger to you from heaven, and he himself immediately hastened into your embrace.

If, then, most revered Lady, the Creator of visible and invisible things so desired your love and so longed for your embrace, with how much love ought we wretched people—who through you have been restored and freed from everlasting death—to love you? With how much reverence ought we to serve you? With how many praises ought we to exalt you?

For you are more beautiful than the sun in appearance, more beautiful in faith, more venerable in grace, and more elegant than all the beauty of women. Therefore, since you are beautiful and comely, lovable and gracious, radiant, shining, and serene, glowing, splendid, and crystalline, I ask you graciously to deign to receive the carbuncle as an adornment of your noble crown, which I have resolved to place in its thirteenth position [Supplement: “place”].

For the carbuncle illumines darkness and flashes brilliance into the eyes of the beholder. You work this in us more effectively, since you are the singular and beautiful Mother of Christ. Who could adequately express the light of your mercies, which you, Lady, have poured into the dark world? Who could adequately recount the virtues and miracles, the great signs and wonders, which you have deigned to perform in many ways and by many means, whether for the salvation of souls, the healing of bodies, the consolation of the good, or the correction of the wicked?

Neither the sweetness of your mercy, nor the abundance of your piety, nor the richness of your grace and goodness is hidden from any Christian, as each person knows from experience that you are present in tribulations, needs, and dangers. Therefore it is delightful for everyone to praise, bless, and proclaim Mary.

When Mary is named, breasts are beaten, heads are bowed, tears of piety or devotion appear, and sighs arise from a contrite spirit or inflamed affection. O name brighter than the sun, more fragrant than balsam and cinnamon! At its utterance the world rejoices, heaven smiles, the angel exults, the just rejoice, the devil is confounded, and hell trembles.

Moreover, if anyone opens the eyes of the heart to behold or consider the perfection of your holiness, the constitution of your body, or the depth of your wisdom and understanding, an exultation of mind, a jubilation of heart, and a serenity of breast are immediately poured forth, or the operation of some spiritual grace. [Note: Our manuscript reads “or opening.”]

## Prayer

O most merciful one, who breathe life into the dead, salvation into those who perish, light into the blind, comfort into the despairing, and consolation into those who mourn! From the treasures of your deepest mercy, I beg you, pour into me jubilation of heart [Note: Alva, “into the heart’s jubilation”], joy of mind, and brightness of breast.

Be my life and the salvation of my soul, the sweetness and peace of my heart, the pleasantness and joy of my spirit. Most radiant Star of the Sea, most compassionate Mother, guide me; defend me from all enemies and dangers, so that, with your grace assisting and your mercy helping, cleansed from every vice and freed from every adversity, I may pass unharmed through this wretched present life and come safely to everlasting joys. Amen.

## Chapter XV. The sun, a most brilliant luminary, illumines the entire crown here

[Col. 0304A]

Seal of chastity, lily of virginity, Mary, more beautiful than women, more delightful than all the angels, holier than all the saints, richer in compassion, more elegant than every grace: the archangel greets you; God the Father sanctifies you; the Holy Spirit overshadows you; the Son of God betroths you. Your soul conceived him in faith through holiness [F., “the holiness of your soul”]; the purity of your womb chastely bore him; the virginity of your body brought him forth in flower.

O glorious and supremely glorious! O praiseworthy and supremely praiseworthy! Who could express your merits, worthily praise your proclamations, or enumerate your merits?

You gave joy to heaven [Note: Our manuscript reads “glory”]; you offered God to the earth; you poured peace back into the world. Through you light is infused into the blind; faith rises in hearts; vices are put to sleep; demons are confounded; Tartarus is emptied; heavenly things increase; the poor are refreshed; the weak are sustained; the humble are exalted; the sick are restored; penitents are illumined; through you the infernal regions are closed and the heavenly realms opened.

From what has been said, most radiant Lady, it is clear that you have attained the blessing and praise of all, because you have poured your benefits upon all. Therefore the patriarchs desire you; the apostles embrace you; the evangelists revere you; the martyrs venerate you; the confessors proclaim you; virgins surround you; angels glorify you; and all together exalt you.

But I, a sinner, who am like none of them [Note: “in” is absent from Alva’s edition], offer you, Lady, for your praise, glory, and honor, the sun, beautiful and shining above all luminaries, so that through me it may be placed in the fourteenth position of your noble crown, so that your crown may thereby be made more radiant and illumined and adorned with more abundant beauty.

For the sun possesses height in its position, agility in its motion, delightfulness in its appearance, fruitfulness in its effect, and luminosity in its activity. Since all these qualities suit you greatly, I have resolved rightly to insert and place the sun in your crown.

For you, Lady, are exalted on high, because your conduct was removed from sinners. Indeed, you established your nest in the heights of heaven; you lifted your heart toward that pure and unbounded light [Note: Alva printed “circumscribed” from his own text, noting that “uncircumscribed” should be read, as we find in the manuscript], the fountainhead of all things. With a dove’s and an eagle’s eye you contemplate God the Father of lights, adoring the divine mystery through ardent desire, expressing the incense of charity and devotion, drinking and tasting from the torrent of divine delight, and from the sweetness of inward pleasantness.

You also move with agility because of your piety. For you travel around the circuit of heaven and earth to see the needs of the poor, the sighs of the young, the pains of the old, the laments of widows, the illnesses of the sick, and the vows of those who serve you, so that, as patroness of the human race and singular physician for the afflicted [Note: Our manuscript reads “medicine”], you may come to the aid of all by the divine gift, through the office of your great mercy and tender-hearted affection.

You also bring, Lady, joy to those who look upon and contemplate you [Note: Our manuscript, “new joy”], because you are beautiful to behold, lovable to contemplate, and delightful to love. The sun and moon marvel at your beauty; the stars are illumined by your splendor; the angels serve your authority [Note: Alva, “purity”].

But who, like you, makes barren souls so fruitful? Who so enriches dry hearts? Who so warms cold breasts? All the good things that supreme Majesty has determined to accomplish there, it has willed to entrust to your hands. For the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, the jewels of spiritual gifts, the adornments of virtues, and the ornaments of graces have been committed to you.

Therefore, when you sow these goods upon us, you make our barrenness fruitful, so that we produce works of salvation [Col. 0305A] and propagate excellent fruits. How many robbers have you made penitents! How many prostitutes chaste and continent! How many plunderers devout almsgivers! How many drunkards temperate and sober! How many gluttons abstinent and moderate! How many lustful people have you made chaste! [Note: “How many angry people have you made gentle!” These words are absent from Alva’s edition.] How many angry people have you made gentle!

You are also radiant and splendid, wholly luminous. For, clothed with light as with a garment, with a crown of twelve stars shining upon your head and the solar mantle in which John saw you gleaming, you clearly revealed to us that, just as the sun rises upon the world in the highest places of God, so the appearance and beauty of your radiance [Note: “is” is absent from Alva] is an adornment of the heavenly Jerusalem, triumphant and militant.

Therefore, just as it is sweet and delightful for the eyes of those who look upon them to see the sun, so it is exceedingly joyful and pleasant for all the angelic hosts to behold your brightness. For this reason, the angels marvel at your most pure radiance; the archangels, at your most perfect holiness; the principalities, at the superiority to be generated [Note: Our manuscript reads “superiority to be generated”; Alva conjectured “general superiority”]; the powers, at your restrainable might; the virtues, at your wondrous operation; the dominations, at your triumphal victory; the thrones, at your most peaceful tranquility; the cherubim, at the ray of your shining wisdom; and the seraphim, at the spark of your burning love.

## Prayer
Although so many miracles are proclaimed concerning you, Lady, I ask that you pour your love into me. Show me your angelic and gracious countenance, so that I may die rejoicing, supported by great hope and confidence, and secure [Suppl.: *de*, “of”] in my corruption and in unfading glory. Amen.

## CHAPTER XVI. The placing of the precious emerald in the Virgin’s crown

Throne of the wisdom of the holy Trinity, most worthy chair of God the Father’s Son, our Lord Jesus Christ; virginal mother and beautiful bride: you, Lady, after God, are my salvation, my hope, and my consolation. In you the abundance of all good things has been stored up for me. [Col. 0305C] You are my anchor amid the waves, my harbor in shipwreck, my support in tribulation, my help in need, my moderation in prosperity, my joy in expectation, and my refreshment in labor. [Col. 0305D: Alva has *naufragium*, “shipwreck.”]

Show yourself, then; come cheerfully to me, daughter of the highest King, sweetness of my soul, light of my mind, peace and serenity of my heart. Let them see you, joy of the angels, restoration of the lost, crown of the virginal lilies. Let them recognize you, hope of penitents, light of minds, fountain of all good things, crown of the triumphant. Appear to me, consoler of my soul, health of my heart, way of my salvation. May I embrace you with holy and chaste desires, Virgin, lily of chastity, foremost example of virginal purity. [Col. 0305D: Alva has “through the merits of virginal purity.”]

And because I have resolved to honor your beauty and loveliness, I ask you, Lady, to deign to accept, for your praise and glory, the precious stone emerald, which I have decided to place in the fifteenth position of your crown. [Col. 0305D: Alva has *quod*, “which.”] For the emerald is a precious stone, dear and beautiful, calm in its green color and pleasing to the eyes. In this, Virgin, you greatly resemble it, queen and eastern star. For what creature was ever dearer and more precious to God, more useful to the world, or more necessary to the human race? [Col. 0305D: The manuscript reads *nunquam*, “never”; the same reading appears in Alva.] You are not merely more precious than precious stones, but also than all women, the sun, the moon, and the stars of heaven, the angels, and all the saints.

You are also the fruit-bearing tree in the midst of paradise, which, watered by the stream of a spring, grows strong, flowers, puts forth leaves, and bears fruit: you grow strong in the budding of good morals, flower in the manifestation of virtues [Col. 0306D: Alva printed *imploratione* (“entreaty”) on his own authority, but conjectured that perhaps *in ploratione* (“in weeping”) should be read], put forth leaves in the spreading of piety, and bear fruit in works of holy charity. [Col. 0306D: Our manuscript reads “the living, irrigating stream of the spring.”] Your verdure brightens the eyes of mind and body, the virtue of your leaves refreshes the languishing, the fragrance of your flowers raises the dead, and the sweetness of your fruits saves penitents and the despairing. [Col. 0306D: Alva has “O Virgin, your eyes.”]

### Prayer

Therefore, my Lady [Col. 0306D: Alva has “glorify”], brighten the eyes of my mind with your gracious verdure; refresh my soul with your holy sweetness; raise me, though dead, by your wondrous fragrance. May I possess you wholly in the midst of my heart and in the secret places of my breast, O light of the world, splendor of the Church, joy of Jerusalem, glory of our people. Pour your most ardent love into my inward parts, so that I may burn to praise you, glorify you, speak of you, and preach about you.

Let your voice sound, glorious Lady, in my ears (Song 2:14); let me feel the veins of your whispering. Show me your most beautiful face, and my soul shall be saved. And since all your inward parts are full of piety and mercy, and since after God you are our unique refuge [Col. 0306D: Alva has “and thus after God”], I ask you graciously and devoutly to hear the lament of the sorrows by which we are afflicted and the distresses by which we are tormented. For today peace has vanished from the earth; human nature languishes and perishes from hunger; Christian despoils and kills Christian. Crops and harvests are devoured by wild beasts, and vineyards are destroyed by them. Vices sprout daily, sins accumulate daily; demons roam here and there, and great earthquakes occur in various places. Piety and mercy have ceased among the laity, honesty and chastity among the clergy; greed and irreverence reign among religious people. Seculars amass gold and silver, while religious also seek and desire these same things.
