The wolf acted like a lamb, and the lamb was disguised as a wolf; falsehood was made to appear truth, and truth was represented as falsehood. Everything concerning the Church has been thrown into confusion.

Since matters stood thus, and impiety was devouring piety, we were led to cry out directly in the manner most fitting for us. We raised the eye of our understanding to the one wise God, the knower of such things, and from him we sought the solution of our difficulties through many prayers.

Therefore, enlightened by the Spirit that comes from him, we determined to summon the eyes of the Church—that is, the priests—to the understanding of the truth. So greatly did we labor for the faith, and so intensely did we strive for piety, caring above all for the condition of the Church, that although surrounded by military concerns and drawn in opposite directions by military plans, we did not grow weary of gathering this most holy synod, so that, once the division of the Churches had been driven away, the bond of peace might be joined together. [Col. 0398A]

For we believe that our entire Christ-loving Roman polity would make peace with the peace of the faith, and indeed your most venerable council was assembled. You too were present with the ecumenical chief shepherd, sharing his theological confession both in spirit and in writing. For we received both the letters sent by his Beatitude and the letters sent by Your Holiness. They were brought forward and read; they set forth the word of truth in proper form and delineated the character of orthodoxy. For in every respect they reproduced, without alteration, the teachings of the synodal and patristic authorities.

We did not neglect them, but carefully compared them. Therefore, all of us, in agreement both in mind and in speech, trusted the one and confessed the other; and we revered Agatho’s document as the very voice of that divinely inspired Peter. For no one disagreed except one. No one among all was lost except the son of perdition, the father of disobedience—and he was torn away, together with his disciples, from the angel-like and most holy choir.

At the proper time we join our lament to that of the prophet, since we too have suffered with him:

“How you have fallen from heaven, O morning star, who rose at dawn, and who were appointed to illumine with the light of unfailing knowledge the souls of believers arranged beneath you, from the height of the priesthood! You who, borne aloft upon the clouds of your airy doctrines, were eager to establish the throne of arrogance! [Col. 0398C] How did you flee from the angel-imitating company of so many priests, and on the wing of madness rise to the deepest fall? Why did you desert the mystical table and emulate the Jewish apostasy? How did you refuse the exhortation of brothers who had assembled a royal and apostolic gathering? How did you, the beloved, kick away those who loved you and urged you toward repentance? Does the one who falls not rise, or is the one who turns away not turned back? Why did you turn away with shameless apostasy, become captive to your heretical purpose, and refuse to return to piety? Surely you were ashamed when convicted of the evil things you had taught.”

O madness combined with blindness! The two seem to be the same. The one causes the body’s footsteps to wander, while the other causes the soul’s steps to stray. He was not ashamed to teach what was wrong, but was ashamed to learn what was right. Such was Macarius, formerly president of the Antiochene Church, the unblessed Macarius, and those who with him defected from the commander’s ranks of Christ. By the vote of that ecumenical assembly they were expelled from priestly dignity and referred to the judgment of the most holy pope.

The holy synod enacted a venerable and respected Definition, agreeing with and following the holy synods and the select Fathers. Our imperial power also subscribed to it and confirmed it through our pious decrees. Through it, by your prayers, the entire fullness of the Church was brought to peace. [Col. 0399A]

Where, then, are those who devised the stumbling block of the shattered heresy? Where are those who clothed themselves in feigned piety as a pretext for false teaching? The trimmings have been stripped from the masks; the fabrications of the deceivers have been exposed; the wolf has removed the hide, and a naked wolf is led forth. He remains visible as what he was hiding by not appearing.

Hypocrisy has been condemned; truth governs; falsehood has been banished; the sower of the weeds [possibly: “weed-like”] doctrines has been cut down. [Col. 0399B] The wheat—the Christ-loving people—has been brought into one granary, namely, the Church of Christ. The light of orthodoxy has risen; the darkness of error has sunk away. Dejection has been transformed, mourning into gladness, gloom into joy; everything has passed over to what is better.

Therefore, we too, rejoicing with the Churches of God that have received the grace of peace, address you in apostolic fashion: “Rejoice, rejoice, and again I say, rejoice”; for the Trinity has granted us a threefold joy.

Farewell, most holy defenders of piety, and pray on behalf of our empire.

And the imperial hand: “We have read.” [lacuna] [Col. 0399C] [lacuna]

[Note: [Col. 0399D] Letter. Baronius judges this letter to be spurious at the cited place. First, because toward the end of May, in the tenth indiction [read: eleventh, MANSI], it is presented as a reply to the emperor’s letter, which he admits he received in July of the same indiction; unless these passages are corrupt, they plainly contradict one another. Second, because there could have been no pontiff in July who was created in August and administered the pontificate for only ten months. [Col. 0400D] Third, because he professes to have written this letter in the tenth indiction, when he had not yet been made pontiff. Fourth, because he writes that Honorius died in the Monothelite heresy and was therefore condemned by a just sentence of anathema, although the Roman Church buried him with a public funeral among the holy pontiffs in the church of Saint Peter, and in every respect performed memorial rites for him as a Catholic pontiff. SEV. BIN.]

## Letter III: Leo II to the Emperor Constantine

[Col. 0400]

Copy of the report sent by Leo, most holy and most blessed pope of elder Rome, to Constantine, the most pious and Christ-loving emperor, confirming and approving what was done and defined in the holy and universal Sixth Council.

[Col. 0400C]

To the most pious and tranquil lord, victor and triumphator, beloved son of God and of our Savior Jesus Christ, the Emperor Constantine: Leo, bishop and servant of the servants of God.

[Col. 0399D] To the King of kings, in whose power are the kingdoms of the world, we, small and great alike, give thanks: he has bestowed an earthly kingdom upon you in such a way as to grant that you might love heavenly things more. For it is greater that, with your mind fixed upon God, you trust in him than that you reign by the honor divinely bestowed upon you. The former benefits you; the latter benefits your subjects entirely.

For by birth, through heavenly mercy, you possess the triumphal glory of your father’s diadem. Your piety is the fruit of mercy, while power is the guardian of discipline. Through the former, therefore, the royal mind is joined to God; through the latter, judgment is exercised over subjects. The wealth of the former assists the needy; the prudence of the latter corrects those who deviate from the true path.

For the concern of rulers in correcting what is wrong is no less than in triumphing over adversaries, because by serving they submit their power to the one by whose gift and protection they are known to rule. Hence your most Christian piety, divinely preordained, preparing in the hidden place of your heart a most worthy dwelling for the Holy Spirit, shows by embracing the Lord Jesus Christ, the head of the Church and rule of true piety, that he is the author of the kingdom granted to you by him. In the same way, by giving and cherishing his holy and venerable body, which is the holy mother Church, as a sincere and principal son, you make it rejoice in unshaken stability. [Col. 0401B]

It is written of you, most merciful of princes, and of that same holy Church spread throughout the whole world: “Kings shall be your foster fathers” (Isa. XLIX). Likewise it is written: “The honor of the king loves judgment” (Ps. XCVIII). Since you place divine matters before human affairs and incomparably prefer the orthodox faith to worldly concerns, what else are you doing than venerating God’s righteous judgment and sacrificing to his invisible majesty, upon the altar of your breast, the purest sacrifice and a whole burnt offering blazing with the fragrance of divine sweetness?

We confidently believe, through the working of God’s grace, that these things may rightly be said concerning the purpose of your most pious mind, most Christian of emperors. By that grace alone every error has been conquered, and the rectitude of the evangelical and apostolic faith, joined to sincere love, prevails among all the leaders of Christ’s Churches. For the truth of the Christian faith shines where the twofold love—of God and of neighbor—burns fervently.

Therefore, unless almighty God, the King of kings, had determined to bestow both of these upon his priests, royal nobility would never bend itself toward its lowliest servants, nor, setting aside for a little while the royal height, desire to be counted as one of the company of priests out of zeal for God. O what glorious, lofty, and true humility, which has deemed it worthy, for divine love, to bow itself down!

What, then, remains, most august, royal, and exalted prince, except that God, who gives increase, may graciously inspire these works in your royal heart, increase them, and complete in you the light of Catholic doctrine, by which the clouds of heretical wickedness may be driven away?

Finally, we received with great joy and rejoicing in the Lord the legates of this apostolic see, your mother, the Roman Church—your piety’s servants: Theodore and George, priests and our sons; John, deacon and our son; and Constantine, subdeacon and regionary of our holy Church—together with the persons who had traveled with them, who, at the command of your piety, had been sent there by my predecessor, of apostolic memory, Pope Agatho, during the eighth indiction on the matter of the faith. They arrived during the recently elapsed tenth indiction, in the month of July, with the imperial letters of your clemency and the synodal acts. [Col. 0404A]

Rejoicing in the Lord with great delight, and as though we had entered the desired harbor of calm after some waves of sorrow, we recovered our strength and began to cry out with thanksgiving: “Lord, save our most Christian king, and hear him on the day on which he calls upon you” (Ps. XIX). Through his God-inspired zeal, the piety of apostolic and true tradition burns throughout the whole world, while the foul darkness of heretical wickedness has vanished.

It is therefore fitting to sing with the prophet and say: “Lord, in your strength the king shall be exalted [or: rejoice], and in your salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly. You have granted him the desire of his heart, and you have not withheld from him the request of his lips” (Ps. XX).

For “a king who sits on a throne,” as a certain very wise man says, “by his gaze scatters every evil” (Prov. XX). Indeed, with the Lord cooperating, the evil that the devil’s wickedness had introduced for the deception of human beings has been scattered by the labors of your piety, and the good of the Christian faith, which Christ bestowed for the salvation of humanity, prevails.

Accordingly, reviewing the sequence of the synodal acts, and requesting each detail with painstaking care, we found that the things narrated by the legates of the apostolic see agreed with the corresponding written records. For we learned that the holy, universal, and great Sixth Council, recently assembled in the imperial city by God’s grace and by imperial decree, held and decreed the same things as the universal council that was seated with this holy apostolic see, whose ministry we perform. [Col. 0404C]

It confessed with us, under the integrity of orthodox faith and according to the rules of the Fathers, that our Lord Jesus Christ is one of the holy and inseparable Trinity, existing from two natures and in two natures, without confusion, without separation, and without division; truly perfect God and perfect man, the same one; while the property of each of the natures united in him remains intact, the same one working divine things as God and human things inseparably as man, without sin alone. It therefore proclaimed that he truly possesses two natural wills and two natural operations. Through these, above all, the reality of his natures is demonstrated, so that the distinction of the natures may be recognized—those natures from which and in which the one and same Lord Jesus Christ subsists.

[Note: [Col. 0403] As in the same Leo’s Letter to the Bishops of Spain. HARD.]

By these things we truly proved that this holy, praiseworthy, and celebrated Sixth Council, through the mercy of God who reveals the truth of the Christian faith to his faithful, followed the apostolic preaching without stumbling, agreeing in all things with the definitions of the five holy and universal councils. It added or subtracted nothing from the established orthodox faith, but walked most directly along the royal and evangelical path. In these matters and through them, the form of the sacred doctrines and the teaching of the distinguished Fathers of the Catholic Church were preserved, and the canonical standard was brought forward for the edification of all. [Col. 0405A]

This too is truly worthy and pleasing to God: the truth of the apostolic preaching, which adorns imperial power and preserves princely clemency, has spread throughout the whole world through the edict of your most august piety and, like a ray of the sun, illumined the hearts of all people, so that they might once again receive the teaching of piety spiritually from the place from which they recognize that the governance of a just administration is kindly provided for them.

Therefore, by the synodal decision and the authority of the imperial edict, like a two-edged sword of the Spirit, the error of the new wickedness was struck down together with the ancient heresies. The authors of falsehood were overthrown along with the stain of their blasphemy—those who had attempted with sacrilegious speech to assert one will and one operation in the two natures of our Lord Jesus Christ, united according to hypostasis, from which and in which he subsisted indivisibly and without confusion.

This norm of the right and apostolic tradition was proclaimed by my predecessor, Pope Agatho, of apostolic memory, together with his synod. He sent it to your piety in a document of his petition, conveyed through his legates, approving and confirming it by the testimonies of the holy and reputable teachers of the Church. The holy and great council now celebrated, with the favor of the Lord and of Your Majesty, received it and embraced it in all respects with us, recognizing in it the sincere teaching of blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, and handling in it the marks of uncorrupted piety.

The holy, universal, and great Sixth Council, which your clemency diligently convened by God’s will and over which you presided in God’s service, followed the apostolic teaching in all things and the doctrine of the reputable Fathers. Since, as has been said, it proclaimed the definition of the true faith in the fullest manner—the definition that the apostolic see of the blessed apostle Peter, whose ministry we perform though unworthy, has reverently received—we too, and through our office this venerable apostolic see, agree harmoniously and unanimously with what it defined and confirm it by the authority of blessed Peter, as upon the firm rock, which is Christ, receiving firmness from the Lord himself.

Therefore, just as we receive and firmly proclaim the five holy and universal councils—the Council of Nicaea, the Council of Constantinople, the First Council of Ephesus, the Council of Chalcedon, and the Council of Constantinople—which the whole Church of Christ approves and follows, so too we receive with equal veneration and judgment the holy Sixth Council recently celebrated in the imperial city through the pious zeal of Your Serenity, as following them and interpreting them. We decree that it is rightly to be numbered with them as having been assembled by the one and equal grace of God, and we likewise judge that the priests of Christ who faithfully assembled in it are to be enrolled among the holy Fathers and teachers of the Church.

For in these men, as in those others, the same Spirit of God worked the salvation of souls. The unfading fruit of this work will be reckoned by the Lord to your imperial piety, whose completion was achieved through your labor, with the grace of God wonderfully cooperating, and whose praise will be proclaimed throughout the ages.

Furthermore, we anathematize and execrate all heresies and all their authors and supporters who, deceived by the devil’s frauds and acting against the apostolic and orthodox faith, attempted to introduce errors of falsehood into the Church—namely: Arius, Sabellius, Macedonius, Apollinaris, Eunomius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Dioscorus, Timothy, Severus, Themistius, Origen, also called Adamantius, Didymus, and Evagrius; likewise the writings of Theodoret against the Twelve Chapters of Saint Cyril, together with the letter called that of Ibas, sent to Maris the Persian; and along with them Jacob, Theodosius [G.: Theodore], Gaianus, Anthimus, Zoaras, Donatus, Novatus, Priscillian, Paul, Photinus, Pelagius [G.: Celestius, Julian], Faustus, and Maximus. The holy Catholic and apostolic Church, as weeds from the threshing floor of the Lord’s Church, cast them out from the catalogue of the faithful Fathers through the winnowing fan of divine judgment, to be consigned to the punishment of Gehenna. [Col. 0408B]

Likewise we anathematize the inventors of the new error: Theodore, bishop of Pharan; Cyrus of Alexandria; Sergius; Pyrrhus; Paul; Peter, successors in the Church of Constantinople—rather, usurpers than overseers [subsessores, that is, “plotters” rather than “presiders”]—and also Honorius, who did not illumine this apostolic Church with the doctrine of apostolic tradition, but attempted by profane betrayal to overthrow the undefiled faith [G.: “allowed the undefiled faith to be defiled”]. We likewise anathematize all who died in their error, and abhor and anathematize their imitators and accomplices, both those of former times and those who remain to this day: namely, Macarius, formerly the most deceitful deceiver of the Church of Antioch, together with Stephen, the disciple of his error—or rather its teacher—and with them the new Polychronius, truly a Simon. Deceived by the phantom of heretical wickedness, he promised to raise the dead; but when the result did not follow his vain presumption, he was shown to be deceitful in this as in everything else.

We also anathematize those who have held or now hold similar opinions, and those who have dared or dare to say that there is one will and one operation in the two natures of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom the holy universal Sixth Council mentioned above rejected. It stripped Macarius of his episcopal dignity, deprived his disciple Stephen and the utterly vain old man Polychronius of priestly honor, and rejected their associates and companions, who “would not understand in order to do good, but meditated iniquity upon their beds” (Ps. XXXV), especially those who attempted to scatter the errors of Macarius here and there.

While hiding beneath the covering of a sheepfold, the wolf appeared; instead of a shepherd, he was found to be a thief and robber, and he was cast out by the true shepherd of the sheep, Christ, as a pestilential destroyer.

Therefore they were rightly struck by the weapon [or: shaft] of the anathema. Bound with eternal chains, because they refused to repent, they are held fast in unbreakable confinement, lest they again, stirred to the audacity of unbridled presumption, infect any of the simple with the contagion of their pestilential teaching. Even now they preferred to persist obstinately in their stubbornness rather than turn back to the knowledge of the truth and be saved through repentance. [Col. 0409A]

Their hearts were hardened by long-standing wickedness, and all saw that they had been overthrown by the stain of conscience rather than by ignorance [variant: “by calamity”]. They were voluntary rebels against apostolic truth, seeking their own glory rather than God’s, although God warns and exhorts sinners toward correction through repentance: “I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezek. XVIII).

For, since your piety graciously deigned through your imperial letters to remind our lowliness that they should be instructed in the doctrines of orthodox faith and salutary teaching, so that they might attain knowledge of sound faith, we diligently extended the hand of spiritual instruction to those who were sick and shipwrecked concerning the faith, that they might reach the harbor of truth. We continually supplied medicinal admonitions for recognizing the rectitude of sound knowledge, and, as befitted our ministry, did not fail to offer the remedies of admonition to those who desired them.

Although the style of writing is not sufficient to recount the admirable struggles of your clemency and your singular vigilance on behalf of the evangelical and apostolic faith, this does not mean that the insignia of your courage should be passed over in silence, since the whole world everywhere proclaims them.

O holy mother Church, rise up; lay aside the garment of mourning and clothe yourself in the robe of your joy. Behold your most steadfast son among princes, your defender and your helper. Do not be shaken: he has girded himself with the sword, the word of God, by which he divides unbelievers from believers; he has put on the breastplate of faith and the helmet of the hope of salvation.

Behold your champion, the new David. Trust; do not fear. He is not that king of one Jewish nation, but this most pious prince of your Christian people, robed in purple by the blood of the Nazarene. He struck down your boastful enemy Goliath and scattered his entire army in every direction. He struck his forehead with the blow of a stone (1 Kings XVII), where there was no seal of piety; his head was cut off, and no strength remained in his limbs.

Behold, triumph is carried everywhere upon a spear. Gather together and come, O most religious Churches of Christ, peoples spread throughout the whole world together with your priests. Sing in a loud voice and say: “The new David, the most steadfast of the emperors, has conquered”—not merely in thousands, for no one could encompass numerically the universal victory of evangelical preaching—but he also destroyed the very prince, enemy, commander, and instigator of all evils, the devil, together with his legions and supporters, by the arms of true, orthodox, and apostolic tradition and confession.

Rejoice now, secure in your freedom, holy mother Church, often attacked but never abandoned. Your unconquered king, Christ, has raised up for you a most pious prince as your champion, benefactor, and lavish provider. Through his zeal, orthodox faith, gathered into renewed splendor, illumines the whole world. All the faithful rejoice, offering thanks; sorrow and humiliation weigh down and confound the unbelieving. The Churches of Christ, freed from every oppression, breathe again; they are cherished by imperial gifts and fortified by princely protection. To them your august piety, imitating Christ, promises in the Lord’s own words: “Behold, I am with you until the consummation of the age” (Matt. XXVIII).

May the Lord Jesus Christ, whose example he follows, grant him possession of Christ’s eternal kingdom and everlasting glory, and may his rule be spread universally and perpetually throughout the world.

May your royal magnanimity graciously deem worthy of reception Constantine, the subdeacon and regionary of this holy apostolic see, the humble bearer of this present petition, who recently attended the holy synod held there with the legates of my predecessor, of apostolic memory. May your clemency incline the ear of your piety to his petitions and receive him honorably as a minister.

May heavenly grace preserve the most pious imperial power of our lord and place the necks of all nations beneath it.

Given on the Nones of May, in the tenth indiction.

[Note: [Col. 0411C] In the year 682, when Leo was not yet pope. HARD.]

[“Given … tenth indiction” is absent in the Greek.]

## Greek parallel text

**Copy of the report sent by Leo, most holy and most blessed pope of elder Rome, to Constantine, the most pious and Christ-loving emperor, confirming and approving what was done and defined in the holy and universal Sixth Council.**

[Col. 0399C]

To the most pious and most tranquil lord, victor and triumphant conqueror, beloved child of God and of our Savior Jesus Christ, the Emperor Constantine: Leo, bishop and servant of the servants of God.

[Col. 0399D] To the King of kings, in whose authority are the kingdoms of the world, we, small and great alike, give thanks—to him who has transferred the earthly kingdom to you in such a way that he might deem you worthy to aspire more greatly to heavenly things [L.: “to strive to present you to heavenly things”]. For it is more important that, being fixed upon God, you speak boldly than that you reign through the honor bestowed upon you by God. The former benefits you; the latter benefits those under your authority [L.: “for that benefits you, while this benefits those under your hand”].

For, as you inherit the glory of your father’s diadem, you enjoy it through heavenly compassion; your piety is the fruit of mercy, while authority is the guardian of order. Through the former, therefore, the royal mind is joined to God; through the latter, judgment is maintained among subjects. The abundance of the former assists the poor, while the prudence of the latter [L.: “the intelligence of the latter”] corrects those who have strayed from the true path.

Nor is the rulers’ concern to correct what is faulty any small matter, just as it is to triumph over adversaries; for, as I suppose, by serving they subject their own authority to him under whose protection and by whose gift they reign. Therefore your Christ-loving piety, divinely prefigured, having prepared a worthy dwelling for the Holy Spirit in the hidden place of your own heart, shows that, by embracing the Lord Jesus Christ, the head of the Church and the rule of true piety, it acknowledges him as the author of the kingdom granted to it by him. In equal measure, by sheltering and honoring his venerable body, which is the holy mother Church, as its genuine and principal child, it makes her rejoice in her own unshaken [variant: “unmoved”] strength.

It is written concerning you, most philanthropic of emperors, and concerning that same holy Church existing throughout the whole world: “Kings shall be your foster fathers.” Likewise it is written: “The honor of the king loves judgment.” Since, by preferring divine things to human affairs and choosing the orthodox faith above worldly concerns without attachment to them, what else are you doing than revering God’s judgment and sacrificing to his invisible majesty, upon the altar of your breast, the purest sacrifice and a whole burnt offering emitting the fragrance of divine sweetness?

We confidently believe that these things may clearly be said concerning the purpose of your pious mind, most Christian of emperors, with the grace of God at work. Through that grace alone every error has been conquered, and the rectitude of the evangelical and apostolic faith, together with the bond of sincere love, prevails among all the leaders of the Churches of Christ. For the truth of the Christian faith shines where the twofold love of God and neighbor burns fervently.

Therefore, unless almighty God, the King of kings, had graciously bestowed both of these upon his priests, royal nobility would in no way descend toward its lowest servants; nor, with the royal height set aside for a little while, would it desire, out of zeal for God, to be counted among the company of priests. O what glorious, most lofty, and true humility, which for love of God has deemed it worthy to descend!

What, then, remains, most eminent and most faithful prince of the emperors, except that God, who grants increase, may worthily inspire these labors in your royal heart, increase them, and complete in you the light of Catholic doctrine, so that the clouds of heretical wickedness may be illuminated [L.: “driven away”]?

Then, too, we received with great joy and rejoicing in the Lord the legates of this apostolic throne, your mother, the Roman Church—servants of your piety: Theodore and George, the presbyters; John, the deacon, our children; and Constantine, the subdeacon and regionary of our holy Church—together with the persons who traveled with them, who had also been sent there by my predecessor, Agatho, pope of apostolic memory, during the eighth indiction, at your piety’s command, on the matter of the faith. During the recently elapsed tenth indiction, in the month of June [L.: July], together with the divine letters of your clemency and the synodal records, we received them, rejoicing and exulting in the Lord with great joy and gladness. As though we had come from waves of sorrow into the desired harbor of calm, and had recovered our strength, we began with thanksgiving to cry out:

“Lord, save our most Christian emperor, and hear him on whatever day he calls upon you.” Through his God-inspired zeal, the piety of apostolic and true tradition is rekindled throughout the whole inhabited world, and the foul mist of heretical wickedness has been made void.

It is therefore fitting to sing together with the prophet and say: “Lord, in your strength the king shall rejoice, and in your salvation he shall exult greatly. You have granted him the desire of his heart, and you have not deprived him of the request of his lips.” For “a king sitting upon a throne,” as a very wise man somewhere says, “disperses every evil by his own gaze.” Indeed, with the Lord cooperating with the labors of your piety, the evil that the devil’s wickedness introduced for the deception of human beings has been scattered, and the good of the Christian faith, which Christ granted for the salvation of humanity, prevails.

Accordingly, having reviewed the greatness of the synodal acts, carefully examining them and requesting each of the records, we found that the same things which the legates of the apostolic throne explained corresponded with the agreeing written documents. For we recognized that the holy, great, and universal Sixth Council, recently assembled in the imperial city by the imperial command through God’s grace, agreed with and decreed the same things as the universal council joined to this holy and apostolic throne, whose ministry we perform, in the integrity of the orthodox faith, according to the canons of the Fathers, and confessed together with us, in one mind, that our Lord Jesus Christ is the one of the holy and inseparable Trinity, existing in two natures without confusion, without separation, and without division—truly perfect God and perfect man, the same one—while the property of each of the natures united in him remains intact; the same one performing divine things as God and human things inseparably as man, without sin alone.

For this reason it proclaimed that he truly possesses two natural wills and two natural operations, through which the truth of his natures is principally demonstrated, so that the distinction of the natures may be recognized—those natures from which and in which the one and same Lord Jesus Christ subsists. Through these things we truly demonstrated [L.: “we recognized by experience”] that this holy, praiseworthy, and celebrated Sixth Council, which through God’s compassion reveals the truth of the Christian faith to believers, followed the apostolic proclamation without stumbling, agreeing in all things with the definitions of the five holy and universal councils, embracing their canons, adding nothing and subtracting nothing from what was defined for the orthodox faith, but walking directly along the royal and evangelical path. In these things and through them the form of the sacred doctrines and the teaching of the distinguished Fathers of the Catholic Church were preserved, and the canonical institution of the documents brought forward [L.: “the canonical institution was brought forward”] for the edification of all.

This too is truly worthy and pleasing to God: that the truth of the apostolic proclamation, which adorns the imperial power and preserves royal clemency, has spread throughout the whole world according to the decree of your most venerable piety and, like a ray of the sun, cleansed the hearts of all, so that they might again receive the teaching of piety spiritually from the place from which they ought to recognize that the governance of just administration is graciously provided for them.

Therefore, by synodal decision and the vote of the imperial decree, like the Spirit’s double-edged sword, the error of the new wickedness was pierced along with the ancient heresies, and the leaders of falsehood were overthrown together with their blasphemy—those who attempted with sacrilegious mouth to proclaim one will and one operation in the two natures of our Lord Jesus Christ, united according to hypostasis, from which and in which he subsisted indivisibly and without confusion.

My predecessor Agatho, pope of apostolic memory, proclaimed this pattern of the right and apostolic tradition together with the venerable synod. In the preceding written documents, in the firm document of the venerable report, he sent it to your piety through his own legates, demonstrating and confirming it by the testimonies of the holy and distinguished teachers of the Church. The holy and great council of the Lord now celebrated through your council received it and embraced it in every respect together with us, recognizing in it the sincere teaching of blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, and discerning in it signs of complete piety [L.: “the holy and great council now celebrated through the Lord and your zeal received it”].

The holy, universal, and great Sixth Council, which your philanthropy diligently convened and presided over by God’s assent for the service of God, followed in all things the apostolic canon and the teaching of the distinguished Fathers. Since, as was said above, it proclaimed the definition of the true faith completely—the definition which the apostolic throne of blessed Peter the apostle, whose ministry we perform though unworthy, reverently received—for this reason we too, and through our order this venerable and apostolic throne, agree unanimously and wholeheartedly with what it defined, and confirm it by the authority of blessed Peter, as upon the solid rock, which is Christ, receiving firmness from the Lord himself.

Therefore, just as we receive and firmly proclaim the five holy and universal councils—the one at Nicaea, the one at Constantinople, the First at Ephesus, the one at Chalcedon, and again the one at Constantinople—which the whole Church of Christ confirms and follows, so also we receive with equal reverence the holy Sixth Council recently completed in the imperial city through the pious zeal [L.: “through the pious struggle”] of Your Serenity, as interpreting and following those councils. We decree that it should rightly be numbered with them, as having likewise been assembled by the grace of God, and we judge that the priests of Christ who faithfully assembled in it should likewise be enrolled among the holy Fathers and teachers of the Church.

For in these men, as in those others, the same Spirit of God worked the salvation of souls; and the unfading fruit of this council will be reckoned by the Lord to your pious empire, through whose labor, with the grace of God wonderfully cooperating, it was accomplished and will be proclaimed throughout the ages.

Furthermore, we anathematize all heresies and all their leaders and promoters, who, strengthened by the deceptions of the devil against the orthodox and apostolic faith, attempted to introduce errors of falsehood into the Churches—namely, Arius, Sabellius, Macedonius, Apollinaris, Eunomius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Dioscorus, Timothy, Severus, Themistius, Origen, also called Adamantius, Didymus, and Evagrius; likewise the writings of Theodoret against the twelve chapters of the most holy Cyril, together with the letter called that of Ibas, sent to Maris the Persian; and along with them Jacob, Theodore [L.: Theodosius], Gaianus, Anthimus, Zoaras, Donatus, Novatus, Priscillian, Paul, Photinus, Pelagius, Celestius, Julian, Faustus, and Maximus. The holy Catholic and apostolic Church, having expelled them from the catalogue of the faithful Fathers as weeds from the Lord’s threshing floor—that is, the Church—and having rejected them for the punishments of Gehenna, cast them away through the winnowing fan of divine judgment. [Col. 0407D]

Likewise we anathematize the inventors of the new error: Theodore, bishop of Pharan; Cyrus of Alexandria; Sergius; Pyrrhus; Paul; Peter, the successors in the Church of Constantinople, more usurpers than overseers; and also Honorius, who did not attempt to cleanse this apostolic Church through the teaching of apostolic tradition, but permitted the undefiled faith to be stained by profane betrayal.

We also anathematize all who died in their own error; and likewise we abhor and anathematize their imitators and accomplices, both those who existed long ago and those who remain to this day—namely, Macarius, who became a deceiver of the Church of Antioch, together with Stephen, the disciple of his error, or rather its teacher; and with them the new Polychronius, truly a Simon. Playing with the apparition of heretical wickedness, he promised to raise the dead; but when the result did not follow his vain presumption, he was shown to be a deceiver in every respect.

We also anathematize those who have thought or think as they did, namely, those who dared or dare—or are about to dare—to say that there is one will and one operation in the two natures of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom the aforementioned holy and universal Sixth Council rejected. It cast Macarius out from the dignity of the presidency; it expelled his disciple Stephen and the deluded old man Polychronius from priestly honor; and it rejected their participants and companions, who were unwilling to understand in order to do good but meditated iniquity upon their beds, and who attempted to sow their errors everywhere, especially Macarius.

The wolf, hiding beneath the sheep’s hide, appeared again; instead of a shepherd he was found to be a thief, and as a robber he was cast out by the true shepherd of the sheep, namely Christ, as a besieger and pestilential destroyer. Therefore they were rightly struck by the spear of the anathema, and, bound with eternal chains, are held fast in unbreakable confinement because they refused to repent, lest they rise again and, through the pollution of their own pestilential teaching, infect some of the simpler people with their unbridled audacity. They even now preferred to persist stubbornly in their own resistance rather than turn back to the knowledge of the truth and be saved [variant: “if they should turn back”].

Their hearts were hardened by long-standing wickedness. Before everyone they appeared to have perished through conscience rather than ignorance, voluntarily attacking apostolic truth and seeking their own glory rather than God’s, although the Lord admonishes sinners and urges them toward correction through repentance: “For he does not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live.” [Col. 0411A]

Since your piety deigned through its divine letters to remind our nothingness that they should be instructed in the doctrines of orthodox faith and salutary teaching, so that they might reach knowledge of sound faith, we diligently extended the hand of spiritual instruction to those who were sick and shipwrecked concerning the faith, so that they might reach the harbor of truth. We continually supplied medicinal aids for recognizing the rectitude of sound faith and, in accordance with what was proper to our ministry, did not fail to provide the medicine of admonition to those who were willing.

Although the written form is not sufficient to recount the admirable struggles of your gentleness and the singular vigilance inherently yours for the establishment of the evangelical and apostolic faith, nevertheless the distinguished signs of your courage were not for that reason passed over in silence, since the whole world everywhere proclaims them.

O holy mother Church, arise; lay aside the garment of gloom and put on the robe of your joy. Behold your most steadfast son among emperors, your avenger and your helper. Do not be troubled: he has girded himself with the sword, the word of God, by which he divides unbelievers from believers; he has put on the breastplate of faith and the helmet, the hope of salvation.

Behold your champion, the new David. Do not fear; take courage. He is not that David, king of one Jewish nation, but this David, your most pious king of the Christ-loving people, robed in purple by the blood of the Nazarene. He struck down your boastful enemy Goliath, scattered his entire phalanx everywhere, and struck his forehead with a stone’s blow, where there was no seal of piety; and once his head had been cut off, no strength remained.

And behold, triumph is everywhere celebrated upon a spear. Gather together and assemble, O most God-fearing peoples of the whole world, together with the priests of the Churches of God. Sing with a loud voice, saying: “The new David, the most steadfast of the emperors, has conquered”—not merely in thousands, for no one can encompass numerically the universal victory of evangelical preaching—but he also destroyed the very chief, enemy, leader, and instigator of all evils and of error, the devil, together with his ranks and accomplices, by the weapon of true, orthodox, and apostolic tradition and confession.

Rejoice, then, holy mother Church, secure concerning your freedom, though often attacked and never abandoned. Your unconquered king, Christ, has raised up a Christ-loving king as your champion, your benefactor, and your provider [variant: “good provider”]. Through his zeal, as orthodox faith gathers its renewed splendor, it illumines the whole world; all the faithful rejoice, sending up thanksgiving, while sorrow and defeat overwhelm and confound the unbelievers. The Churches of God have breathed again, freed from all their afflictions; they are cherished by imperial gifts and fortified by imperial protection. To them your most venerable piety, imitating Christ in the Lord’s words, promises: “Behold, I am with you until the consummation of the age.” May he, like the Lord Jesus Christ whose teachings he uses, attain the enjoyment of his eternal kingdom and everlasting glory, and may his dominion be extended universally and eternally throughout the inhabited world.

May your royal magnanimity graciously deem worthy of reception Constantine, the subdeacon and regionary of this apostolic throne, the humble bearer of this report, who recently attended the holy synod celebrated there together with the legates of my predecessor, of apostolic memory. May your royal clemency incline the ear of your benevolence to his reports and receive him honorably as a deacon.

May heavenly grace preserve the pious power of our lord and subject to it the necks of all nations.

[Note: [Col. 0411C] Letter. Baronius rejected this letter, together with the three following ones, as spurious, because throughout each of them it is repeatedly asserted that the ecumenical council was completed in the ninth indiction [ [Col. 0411C] The pope did not say that it was completed in every respect in the ninth indiction, but only that it was celebrated then, which is entirely true. Add that only two sessions, the twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth, already begun at Constantinople in the tenth indiction on 11 and 16 September, were held before the tenth indiction began to be reckoned at Rome and in the West, from 24 September of the same year. MANSI.]—whereas the acts of the final sessions testify that the synod was completed in its tenth session. He rejected it especially because these letters are said to have been sent to Spain not with the synodal acts themselves, but only with the definition of the synod, the emperor’s edict, and the synodal acclamatory address, which [Col. 0413D] are only a small part of the synodal acts. Yet the bishops testify in canon 2 of the Fourteenth Council of Toledo that they received the complete synodal acts together with Leo’s letter. [ [Col. 0413D] That word is absent from the canon; nor could he have sent the acts complete, since, as Leo himself testifies, they had not yet been translated from Greek into Latin. ID.] Therefore the authentic letter of Leo to the bishops of Spain must have been lost, while only spurious and fabricated copies remain. The manuscript copy was communicated to us from the Toledo library by the reverend and distinguished man Lord James Hutter, doctor of sacred theology and priest-canon of the metropolitan church of Cologne; we compared it with the edition of the letters of the Roman pontiffs. SEV. BIN.]

## Letter IV: Leo II to the Bishops of Spain

[Col. 0411C]

It recounts the acts of the Sixth General Council, at which the heretics were condemned and the definition of the Catholic faith concerning the two wills and operations in Christ was promulgated. He sends it so that all may make it known, and so that the bishops themselves may subscribe to it.

To all the most beloved brothers, the bishops presiding over the Churches of Christ established throughout Spain: Leo.

[Col. 0413A] Since human pursuits are various, by which human life is believed to be administered, there is nevertheless one duty of piety that can lead to the gain and reward of eternal life; in this every associate of the Christian faith ought equally to devote himself. The gracious condescension of the Holy Spirit inspires affection for this duty and displays the unimpaired fruit of good works, because the Spirit—as the Lord teaches—“breathes where he wills, and you hear his voice” (John 3), and because his grace is incomprehensible, he joins and attests, and you do not know from where he comes. Therefore, knowing and being assured that there burns in you a fervent devotion to the Christian religion, you embrace with spiritual arms the seeds of heavenly doctrine, and in you the fervor and purity of evangelical and apostolic tradition bear fruit. For this cause the holy apostolic See, mother of all the churches, has always labored and still labors even to the point of sacrifice [Col. 0413B], and, if divine majesty so decreed, would sooner allow the soul to be separated temporarily from the body than, through sacrilegious betrayal, to be separated from a truthful confession for the sake of temporal pleasure or affliction. For apart from this, just as one cannot attain the reward of eternal blessedness that the Lord has prepared for his saints, so—what must be mournfully lamented—one who has been made an exile from the living and true God through the error of a deceitful doctrine is handed over to eternal torments.

But now, by the grace of God, while our most Christian son, the emperor Constantine—whom heavenly clemency has chosen and pre-eminently appointed for this pious duty—reigns, the splendor of right confession and apostolic tradition, the darkness of heretical depravity having been expelled, has shone throughout the whole world like a radiant beam [Col. 0413C]; and peace and concord in the truth reign among all the prelates of Christ’s churches, proceeding from the peaceful confession of Christ, who is true and saving peace, through whom we are reconciled to God.

Let your sincerity know, and let it be made known to all Christians, the wondrous mighty works of almighty God: in the city of Constantinople our most merciful lord—or rather, the emperor, son of blessed Peter the Apostle—armed with zeal for God and inflamed by the desire for piety, assembled bishops from every part of the world. What he had long and faithfully desired, when heavenly majesty so decreed, he fulfilled during the recently elapsed ninth indiction [the ninth]. Thus the holy Sixth Ecumenical Council was celebrated. For its celebration, priests and deacons were sent in the person of our predecessor, the lord Agatho, pope of apostolic memory.

[Note: [Col. 0414D] Here the author of the letter implies that the ecumenical council continued up to his own time; hence it is evident that Leo was not the author of this letter. Baronius, year 683, no. 18. MANSI.]

Concerning the various councils [Note: [Col. 0414D] “Councils” here signifies provinces. ID.] subject to this holy Apostolic See, whose ministry we exercise, archbishops were dispatched by us [Col. 0414A]. They presided and sat together with the pious prince and with all the prelates of the churches who had assembled at his command. First, they read and reconsidered the five holy ecumenical councils and the venerable Fathers of the Church, whose books and testimonies had been sent from here, together with the dogmatic Tome of our predecessor, the lord Agatho, pope and pontiff of apostolic memory, and with the responses of our entire synod, in confirmation of the two natural wills and operations in our one Lord Jesus Christ and in condemnation of those who taught or believed otherwise. Since they investigated the things of God with fear and love of him, by his will the sincerity of the true confession was demonstrated and confirmed through them [Note: [Col. 0414D] Read *verae* (“of the true one”). HARD.]. Accordingly, the synodal definition declares itself consonant with the words of the apostolic men; through these we trust that your devotion will be satisfied.

Those who had rebelled against the purity of apostolic tradition departed indeed under sentence of eternal condemnation: Theodore of Pharan, Cyrus of Alexandria, Sergius, Pyrrhus, Paul, Peter of Constantinople, and Honorius, who did not extinguish the flame of heretical doctrine when it began—as apostolic authority required—but by neglecting it, fostered it. Those survivors who refused to turn back to the confession of the truth through the remedy of repentance were deposed from episcopal and priestly rank: Macarius, formerly bishop of Antioch, together with Stephen, formerly an abbot and priest, his disciple—or rather, the kindler of heretical error—and the former abbot and priest Polychronius, a new Simon [Col. 0414C]. They were deservedly expelled from the churches of Christ as unfaithful hirelings, and, because they had become harmful successors and corrupters, were brought here as exiles, so that they might recognize the reproach of their guilt and their blasphemies against God, having been placed under the contempt and condemnation of all the faithful.

Since the proceedings held in the city of Constantinople during the celebration of the universal council were written in Greek because of the diversity of languages and have not yet been carefully translated into our language, we have meanwhile sent to your devotion, by the bearer of this letter, Peter, regional notary of our holy Church, the definition of that same holy Sixth Council and the acclamation made by the entire council to the most pious prince, which is called the *Prosphoneticus*, as well as the decree of the most merciful emperor, translated from Greek into Latin and sent everywhere for the knowledge of all [Col. 0414D]. We shall also send the proceedings of the entire venerable council once they have been carefully and accurately translated, if your charity, burning with good zeal, also takes pleasure in this.

Therefore we exhort your concord, devoted to the divine ministries in the truth of the faith, to furnish the utmost diligence and effort and to gird yourselves with equal labor for the love and fear of God, for the advancement of the Christian religion, and for the purity of apostolic preaching. Through your devout zeal, let this become known and beneficially proclaimed among all the prelates, priests, and peoples of your province; and let subscriptions by all the reverend bishops be appended with you to the definition of the same venerable council. Let each prelate of Christ’s churches hasten to inscribe his name in the book of life, so that, through the confession of his subscription, he may spiritually assemble with us and with the universal holy synod in harmony with the one evangelical and apostolic faith [Col. 0415A]. Thus, when our Lord Jesus Christ comes in glorious and terrible power to judge, may he meet him bearing the title of orthodox confession and, through the seal of his own hand, show himself a participant in the apostolic tradition. [Note: [Col. 0415D] Cardinal de Aguirre reads from the manuscript: “so that, with the princes of the apostles, whose confession …”]

While he also embraces the confession of Christ’s apostles with zeal for true piety, may he enjoy blessed fellowship, always turning over in the secret places of his heart the saying of the Lord who preached: “Whoever confesses me before men, him I will confess before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10). For we also, although unequal to them, nevertheless exercise the office of the prince of the apostles; and when, with God’s protection, we receive the pages of your subscriptions through the bearer of this letter [Note: [Col. 0415D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript: “your subscriptions in the pages”], we deposit them at the confession of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles [Col. 0415C], so that through him and by his intercession—from whom the true tradition of the Christian faith has descended—the mystery of those who faithfully confess and subscribe may be offered to the Lord Jesus Christ as a testimony and to his glory. He truly has permitted the proclamation of his confession, which for so long had been suppressed by the snares of heretics, to shine everywhere with the clear rays of truth, inspired by the persistent pious zeal of the prince.

Since an opportunity for salvation has been offered, we exhort you to show yourselves making this divine gift truly fruitful through effective diligence, so that your glory before God may increase through purity of conscience. May God keep you safe, most beloved brothers.

[Note: [Col. 0415D] Letter. Baronius infers that it is a forgery from the name Quiricus, for no other bishop of Spain bearing this name is found except Quiricus, bishop of Toledo, who died seven years earlier and had Julian as his successor; Julian participated in the Thirteenth Council of Toledo during the time of Leo II. Baronius, in the aforementioned year, no. 19. SEV. BIN.]

## EPISTLE V. LEO II TO QUIRICUS, BISHOP

[Col. 0415D]

He writes that he has sent Peter with a letter; Peter conveys the synod’s definition and certain gifts.

To his most beloved brother Quiricus, Leo.

We bring to the knowledge of your true devotion that we have hastened to send there the bearer of this letter, Peter, regional notary of our holy Church [Col. 0416A], with a *tractoria* to all the prelates of Christ’s churches together with us, and also to our most excellent and most Christian son, the king, to the glorious count, providing him also with responses concerning the definition [Note: [Col. 0416D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript, emends it thus: “and to the glorious count as well: let them also provide responses,” etc.] of the venerable synod, which, during the recently elapsed ninth indiction, was celebrated in the city of Constantinople with God’s protection for the stability of our orthodox faith. He also brings the acclamation of the most reverend bishops assembled there and the decree of our most pious son and most merciful emperor.

For the sake of God’s ministry, which we have undertaken, and of the rectitude of apostolic faith—through which we hope that both we and the souls entrusted to us may be saved—may your devotion in Christ offer every care and assistance [Col. 0416B], so that, for your fervent devotion to evangelical and apostolic faith, you may deserve to share eternal blessedness with the blessed princes of Christ’s apostles. May God keep you safe, most beloved brother.

As a gift of blessing, therefore, we have sent to your devotion a cross containing a key made from the sacred bonds of our author, the blessed apostle Peter. May the love of God and neighbor bind the episcopal dignity, and may, through the standard of the saving cross [Note: [Col. 0416D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript: “the cross of Christ”], Christ, who was suspended upon it, fasten all the members of his body with the key of the divine commandments, so that, fortified by such a seal [Note: [Col. 0416D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript: “so that, fortified by such a sign”], when the gates of the heavenly kingdom have been opened, the prince of the apostles may receive you to enjoy eternal blessedness with him.

## EPISTLE VI. LEO II TO SIMPLICIUS THE COUNT

[Col. 0416C]

He recounts the proceedings of the council and sends its definition, to which the bishops are to subscribe, asking him to ensure that it be made known to all in his edition.

To the glorious lord, his son, Count Simplicius [Note: [Col. 0416D] His name is not found among the counts who subscribed to the Thirteenth Council of Toledo.], Leo, bishop, servant of the servants of God.

Since the true confession of God, descending from apostolic tradition, is the remedy for your salvation, and since the blessed martyrs, detesting temporal things, earned through it the rewards of eternal life, while the most approved holy Fathers and teachers of the Church chose to surrender their souls rather than betray this true faith, after enduring various struggles and immense afflictions for it, this holy Church of Christ—founded and built up by the prince of his apostles—is known even now to preach this faith from their authoritative teaching. Through apostolic successors, the institution of the Savior has by God’s grace reached us, and our predecessors have labored exceedingly for its stability.

But after so many struggles and countless afflictions inflicted at various times by enemies of the true faith, heavenly clemency at last preserved the imperial heart by heavenly grace [Col. 0417A]. Moved by the fervor of its grace to proclaim the integrity of true piety, it recently decided to assemble a universal council from various parts of the world. The legates of this holy Apostolic Church—which by divine condescension we have undertaken to administer—and representatives of the councils and of those subject to it [Note: [Col. 0417D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript: “and of the council subject to it”], assembled in the same sacred council together with our most serene son, the emperor, crowned with the insignia and diadems of piety. Strengthened by the pontifical writings and testimonies of the holy Fathers, they proved with all their strength [Ms., “with all their might”] that this holy Church, supported by divine aid, should wholly preach and preserve the rule of apostolic tradition.

For the Tome of the lord Agatho, of apostolic memory, the great pontiff and our predecessor [Col. 0417B], which he had sent to the most tranquil emperor, was so furnished with the definitions of the holy councils, the testimonies of the blessed Fathers, and assertions of truth that it most clearly revealed the integrity of the apostolic faith, exposed the hiding places of heretical error, and, through its unassailable statements, caused the darkness of heretical doctrine to be removed from human hearts by God’s grace, so that the light of true confession shone forth. In this the labor of the most gentle prince for the piety of right faith shone brilliantly, worthy of praise throughout all ages, so that, with his favor and God’s protection, the truth of apostolic faith might receive the prize of victory and the empire divinely granted to him might be adorned with the insignia of piety.

Therefore, you also, most glorious sons of Christ’s Church, in whom the desire for piety is strong, extend your hand in support of evangelical [Col. 0417C] and apostolic preaching, so that the radiance of the sincere faith that you love may shine upon your Christian regions. By favoring and assisting apostolic preaching, may you deserve to share the fellowship of the faithful before God, to whom the integrity of true confession is referred.

Since it belonged to our office, to which the administration of souls has been entrusted, we have hastened, with paternal affection, to make known to your provinces and to send there through the bearer of this letter, Peter, regional notary of our holy Church, the definition of the holy Sixth Council, celebrated in the city of Constantinople during the ninth indiction, and the acclamation of all the most reverend bishops, which is also called the *Prosphoneticus*, as well as the edict of faith sent here by our most pious Augustus, our most serene son [Col. 0417D]. Thus you may rejoice unanimously with us as participants in the advancement of evangelical and apostolic preaching and in the merit of true faith.

We have also exhorted all the most reverend prelates of the churches to append their subscriptions to that apostolic synodal definition, and, as fathers for and with their sons, to inscribe their names in this book of life, to the praise of those who faithfully come together and labor with the Gospel of Christ [Col. 0418A], and as a commendation before God, whom we then deserve to have propitious when we preserve his faith unaltered and unharmed to the end. May heavenly grace protect your glory.

For the perpetual protection of your glorious Christianity, we have therefore sent by the present bearer a venerable cross and a key made from the saving bonds of our author, Peter, prince of Christ’s apostles, so that you may be continually saved by the apostolic protection of him whose sincere love you bear, whose lamps you faithfully tend, and whose upright tradition you truthfully embrace.

[Note: [Col. 0417D] This letter is also attributed to Benedict, Leo’s successor, under the title: “Benedict, by the grace of God priest and elect of the holy Apostolic See, to his excellent son, Ervig, lord.” HARD.]

## EPISTLE VII. LEO II TO ERVIG, KING OF SPAIN

Its subject is the same as that of the preceding letter.

[Col. 0418B] To the most excellent lord, his son, Ervig, king, Leo.

Since God alone is king of all, who created everything from nothing and governs and sustains what he created—for he is truly King of kings and Lord of lords—he himself, incomprehensible, by the balance of his providence, disposes that various people reign on earth both in time and in different places. Although their kingdoms are divided, he nevertheless equally demands from each an account of his administration and truly expects from them one offering of praise, the confession of himself. The immensity of his majesty is pleased with the human race by this one gift alone: that all proclaim a true confession of him. Thus, although the arrangements of temporal affairs appear diverse, harmony in unity must be maintained regarding the rectitude of faith in him.

The Savior, the Son of God, also established this in his holy disciples. He appointed blessed Peter prince in place of himself over his disciples; through his saving preaching and tradition, this entire [perhaps, “holy”] apostolic Church of Christ, proceeding as from a fountain of preaching, has led all the regions—including those over which your majesty presides—to knowledge of the truth and to the life of life, and it illuminates the summit of your kingdom [Note: [Col. 0417D] Read from the manuscript, with Cardinal de Aguirre: “and has illuminated it.”]. While you reign by God’s grace in piety, you acquire from your temporal kingdom the kingdom of eternal blessedness. To attain this more perfectly, just as we earnestly pray, so, while by God’s condescension we exercise the office of the fathers and, though unequal, fulfill by divine aid the place of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, in the ministry entrusted to us, we strive by preaching and admonition to advance you toward the reward of blessed life [Col. 0418D].

The beginning of attaining eternal blessedness is the rule of right apostolic preaching. Although certain people formerly attempted to undermine it, endeavoring to introduce heretical errors into the Church of Christ, evangelical truth prevails. For the sake of preserving its subtlety and immutability, this apostolic Church of Christ has always endured and still endures various snares of affliction, and, with heavenly grace assisting it, remains unharmed. [Note: [Col. 0418D] Read from Cardinal de Aguirre’s manuscript, “for whose subtlety and immutability are to be preserved.”]

[Note: [Col. 0418D] This passage clearly proves the letter to be a forgery: the emperor wrote concerning the convocation of the ecumenical council not to Agatho but to Pope Donus, and he sent it not in the ninth indiction but in the sixth, as can be seen from the same sacred letter of the emperor to Donus. MANSI.]

But now—something we joyfully proclaim with thanksgiving to God—during the recently elapsed ninth indiction, our most pious and most Christian lord, indeed the emperor, son of God’s Church, sent imperial letters to our predecessor, Agatho, pope and pontiff of apostolic memory, earnestly exhorting him to send from the holy Church of the Apostolic See, from all the venerable councils connected with it, legates drawn both from the prelates of the churches and from the other ecclesiastical orders, equipped with dogmatic letters and with the books and testimonies of the venerable Fathers, to the royal city of Constantinople. This was accomplished and brought to completion by God’s will.

When these men arrived there from this place, his piety assembled a council from various regions. Setting aside for a little while the cares of the commonwealth entrusted to him [Col. 0419B], he sat in the venerable council of the bishop-brothers and caused the truth of apostolic tradition and the rectitude of faith to be carefully and attentively examined through the holy synods, the testimonies of the venerable Fathers, and the assertions of the aforesaid apostolic pontiffs of ours. He also caused the sincerity of the true faith to be demonstrated by the legates of this holy Apostolic See.

This was begun and completed with the protection of the empire assisting [Note: [Col. 0419D] Cardinal de Aguirre, from the manuscript: “with the support of the empire assisting”], and the truthfulness of our true faith shone forth most perfectly in accordance with the venerable councils and the teachings of approved Fathers. Thus we proclaim that in our one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who is also true and perfect God, and the same true and perfect man, just as we confess two natures inseparably and without confusion—namely, divine and human—so we proclaim that he possesses two natural wills and two natural operations, according to the qualities and properties of the natures converging in him [Col. 0419C].

For although we believe Christ to be one and to be one person of the holy Trinity, we nevertheless proclaim that he possesses both the divine and the human nature, together with the properties of those natures, without confusion, division, or diminution.

The most pious emperor, inspired by the grace of the Holy Spirit and willingly enduring labor for the purity of the Christian faith, strove with all his strength to cleanse the catholic Church of God from the stain of heretical error. Whatever could generate offense among Christian peoples he caused to be removed from the Church of God. All the authors of heretical assertions, condemned by the venerable council [Col. 0419D], were expelled from the unity of the catholic Church: Theodore, bishop of Pharan; Cyrus of Alexandria; Sergius; Paul; Pyrrhus; and Peter, formerly prelates of Constantinople; and, together with them, Honorius of Rome, who consented to allow the unstained rule of apostolic tradition, which he had received from his predecessors, to be stained.

Likewise Macarius of Antioch, together with Stephen, his disciple—or rather, the teacher of heretical depravity—and a certain mad old man, Polychronius, the last [Note: [Col. 0419D] Read “a new Simon,” as above in Leo’s letter to the bishops of Spain, and so Cardinal de Aguirre.] who [Note: [Col. 0419D] Cardinal de Aguirre reads from the manuscript: “who promised to accomplish this by raising the dead, through heretical preaching …”] had recently promised, through the confidence of heretical preaching, to accomplish it [Col. 0420A], and who, confused, refused to turn back again to the way of true confession and salvation [Note: [Col. 0420D] Another reading: “being confined, he wished to turn back.”], was punished with eternal condemnation. All these, together with Arius, Apollinarius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Severus, Theodosius, and Themistius [Note: [Col. 0420D] In place of “Themistius,” the text has “Themesius.” HARD.], were shamelessly attempting to defend the heretical doctrine that there is one will and one operation in the divinity and humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ. For they did not demonstrate this, as priests ought, through the testimonies of the holy Scriptures and the Fathers; rather, by worldly sophistries they craftily sought to pervert the Gospel of Christ.

Divine judgment cast all of them, together with their errors, out of his holy Church. Now, with heavenly protection assisting, all the prelates of God’s churches everywhere agree in one harmony of the true faith. There has become one mouth and one lip, one flock and one shepherd, Christ the Son of God, whom all his priests unanimously and sincerely proclaim.

Therefore, let the dignity of your Christian kingdom also assume the zeal of piety, so that this may be preached to all the churches of God, to prelates, priests, clerics, and peoples, for the praise of God, for the stability of your kingdom, and for the salvation of all. May almighty God be glorified and praised unanimously by all peoples.

We have accordingly arranged to send there, through the bearer of this letter, Peter, regional notary of our holy Church, the definition of the holy council, the acclamation of the most reverend bishops to the most pious emperor—which is called the *Prosphoneticus*—and the decree of the most merciful emperor, composed in confession of the true faith and issued everywhere [Col. 0420C]. Thus, in the definition of the sacred synod sent there by us, all the prelates of the churches of your most devout kingdom, as spiritual fathers for their sons, may each append his subscription according to its wording, as though inscribing it in the book of life through the seal of his confession.

May peace and concord in the churches of God increase and remain during the time of your exalted kingdom, by God’s permission and with your Christian favor. May he who has appointed your majesty to reign grant, supported by the stability of his faith, that the people entrusted to you may be administered prosperously and pleasingly to him for very many years. [Col. 0420D] May heavenly grace keep your excellence safe.

## FRAGMENT OF A LETTER OF LEO II TO THE BISHOPS AND KING OF DALMATIA

If from now on any bishop, priest, or deacon takes a wife, or retains one whom he has taken, let him fall from his own rank until he comes to make satisfaction; nor let him remain in the choir of those singing psalms, nor receive any portion of ecclesiastical property.

## IN THE YEAR OF THE LORD 684. BENEDICT II, ROMAN PONTIFF

[Col. 0421]

## HISTORICAL NOTICE ON BENEDICT II

*(From Mansi, “The Most Extensive Collection of Councils”)*

[Col. 0421A] [Note: [Col. 0421B] Benedict. In the year 684, on the twentieth day of August, Benedict was created pontiff, after the pontifical See had been vacant for one month and twenty-two days. In a letter marked by Christian charity and free from all contention, he admonished the bishops of Spain to correct—or rather, to explain—how, in their letter, which they had returned to the Apostolic See through Peter the regional notary, they asserted three substances in Christ. For the most vigilant prelate of the Church feared that, by this doctrine of theirs, they might establish three wills in the Lord: divine, rational, and sensual, just as they asserted in the same Christ the Lord three substances—one of divinity, another of the soul, and a third of human flesh.

Next, he asked them to explain what they meant when they said in the same letter that “wisdom had begotten wisdom” and “will had begotten will.” He wanted this explained so that no one could suspect that Catholics were professing two wills in Christ. These matters are established from the proceedings of the Fifteenth Council of Toledo.

What the other two chapters were that seemed to Benedict to require more exact clarification, we do not know. Nevertheless, the same Fathers who attended the said council testified that they could be defended according to the teaching of the holy Fathers Ambrose and Fulgentius. The sense in which the Spaniards had asserted the aforesaid second chapter according to the teaching of Saint Augustine is explained by the Master of the *Sentences*, book I, distinction 17, and by St Thomas, *First Part*, question 39, articles 5 and 6.

At the Fifteenth Council of Toledo, in their defense, they said that they had asserted this not according to relation but according to substance. See Garcia, under the entry “Pope Benedict.” Hence it is clear that Benedict was unjustly and calumniously reproached by Roderic, archbishop of Toledo, when he says: “The book on the three substances, which the most holy Julian had long ago sent to Rome, and which Benedict, Roman pope, in treating the matter less cautiously, had ordered to be rejected, because it said that will begot will.”

For Pope Benedict did not reject this assertion of the Spaniards as contained in a book, but as contained in the letter of the Spaniards; he requested that it be explained, and requested that this be done not in writing but orally, by word of mouth, through a certain trustworthy man.

The same Benedict labored with the greatest zeal so that, after the death of Theophanes of Antioch, Macarius, formerly bishop of Antioch, who had been restored to clerical order and was living in exile at Rome, might, after his heresy had been condemned, be restored to the Church of Antioch. But the stubborn man refused. See the first session of the Second Council of Nicaea. SEV. BIN.]

Benedict [Note: [Col. 0421A] Codex Luc., “Benedict the Younger.”], a Roman by nationality, son of John [Note: [Col. 0422B] He sat for ten months and twelve days. From his death, which is commemorated annually in the Church on 7 May, it is inferred that Benedict sat for eight months and seventeen days. ID.], sat for ten months and twelve days [eight months and seventeen days]. From his earliest years he served the Church and conducted himself in the divine Scriptures, in singing from childhood, and in the dignity of the priesthood as befits a man worthy of his name, in whom the grace of true heavenly blessing abounded, so that in name and works alike he might be worthy to attain the administration of the pontificate. He loved poverty; he was humble, gentle, patient [Note: [Col. 0421A] Codex Luc., “having compassion on all,” etc.], and exceedingly generous [“most generous”].

He restored the church of the blessed apostle Peter, as well as that of the blessed martyr Lawrence, which is called Lucina’s. Likewise, in the church of blessed Valentine on the Flaminian Way, he made a covering over the altar with nails and small rods [Note: [Col. 0421A] Codex Luc., “fixed in, and with small rods”] [“fistulas”], and around it a most precious, very broad gold-embroidered border [*palergium chrysoclavum*]. Similarly, in the church of blessed Mary at the Martyrs, he made another porphyry-colored covering with a cross and gems, four gold-embroidered strips, and around it a very beautiful border of *holosericum* [silk]. He also made, in the aforesaid title-church of Lucina, another ornamented silk covering.

He made two ministerial golden chalices, each weighing one pound [Note: [Col. 0422C] Here he received the imperial commands of the most merciful Constantine the Great, etc. The emperor Constantine restored the Roman Church to its former liberty, granting it the right to consecrate its pontiff freely and no longer to await any confirmation by the emperor, which certain Eastern emperors had claimed by the example of the Gothic kings. When the emperor Constantine had conferred this favor upon the Church and had reigned for seventeen years, he died, leaving his son Justinian heir to the empire. Concerning him, see the Life of John V. Anastasius. ID.].

He received the imperial commands of the most merciful Constantine the Great, addressed to the venerable clergy, the people, and the fortunate army of the Roman city. Through these commands the emperor granted that the person elected to the Apostolic See should immediately and without delay be ordained pontiff.

Together with the clergy and the army [Note: [Col. 0422C] “He received locks of hair.” By *mallones* he means locks of hair. For Greek *μαλλός* means the same as Latin *vellus*, “fleece.” What this symbol signified can be understood from a passage of Paul the Deacon, who says in book VI, chapter 15 of the old edition of the *Dialogues*: “About this time Charles, prince of the Franks, sent his son Pippin to Liutprand so that, according to custom, he might receive his hair. Cutting his hair, Liutprand became his father and sent him back to his father, enriched with many royal gifts.” Thus you understand that in those times the custom prevailed that, by such an offering of hair, a person was offered as a son to the one who received it. Hence it is plainly understood that when the emperor Constantine offered the hair of his sons to the pontiff, he wished the Roman pontiff to be honored, loved, and obeyed by them as a parent, and wished them to comply more diligently with his admonitions. See Baronius, year 684, no. 7.], he received the locks of hair of the lords Justinian and Heraclius, sons of the most merciful prince, together with the command by which it was indicated that they had sent those locks of hair.

During his pontificate, a star appeared at night near the vigils [perhaps, “the Pleiades”] in a clear sky during the period between the Nativity of the Lord and the Theophany, completely shrouded, like the moon beneath a cloud [Col. 0423A].
