Behold, both faiths are evident. But for this faith that we defend, we are prepared not only for exile but also to die. The sea is stormy and tossed by waves, but the little ship is not sunk, because faith does not waver.

The rains of the heretics descend, the winds of persecutions blow, and the rivers arrive—that is, the threats and terrors of the heretics. But the house built for a long time upon the firmest rock with squared stones by the craftsman’s hand is not destroyed from its foundation.

And even if an angel should come from heaven intending to implant in us your alien faith, it will be reckoned to us as anathema maranatha.

And because, as we have said, the winds and rivers are already threatening, that house which is undoubtedly founded upon sand will be overturned from its roots. What is sand except heresies? And since there are many heretics, they also fabricate many lies, because they hold diverse opinions against the Catholic faith and yet cannot agree among themselves at all.

Behold the field of the Scriptures and the one Christ—and yet it is divided between the two sides. The side that rightly believes in Christ has what he himself says: “Rivers of living water will flow from his belly.” When it possesses Christ, it will possess the law and the Gospel.

But the side that does not possess Christ cannot have that water flow from him, nor can it direct into itself the rivers that the Holy Spirit has not dictated.

But undoubtedly there is that water which is called “perverse knowledge” in Solomon, through the woman who bears the type of heresy and flatters with crafty persuasions, saying: “Stolen waters are sweeter” (Prov. 9:17).

Let us not write philosophically in obscure expressions, but plainly, so that all who hear may not need to ask one another, but all may understand [Col. 0902D].

### XV.

And since the matter concerns the right faith, it must be proved not by ornate and polished speech but by evident facts. Let each of us draw water from the fountains of the Savior, that is, from the teachings of the prophets and apostles.

Let no one dig for himself new cisterns, concerning which the Lord says through the Prophet: “They have abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water; for the earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord like the waters of the sea” (Jer. 2:13).

To dig a new cistern is to devise new statements about Christ that are not written in the law and the Gospel.

In the Gospel the Lord refers to this cistern in the parable of the unjust steward, who says: “I cannot dig; I am ashamed to beg” (Luke 16:3).

This unjust steward was Saul, who afterward became the apostle Paul. When he was Saul, he was exalted and proud. He gloried in the law and in knowledge of the Scriptures. At the feet of Gamaliel, who at that time was most learned in the law, he boasted that he had learned letters; and for this reason he persecuted Christ’s apostles, saying that they did not know the law and were uneducated.

Therefore, still breathing threats and murder against the Lord’s disciples, he went to the priest and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women who belonged to this Way, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem (Acts 9:2).

When he began to persecute, bind, and kill those who believed in Christ, and to destroy all the substance of his God, the Lord seized him.

“Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad.”

And he said in his heart: “What shall I do? I was a teacher and a steward, and I am forced to become a disciple and a laborer. I cannot dig.”

What did he mean by “I cannot dig”? It was as though he said plainly: “I cannot prophesy beyond what has been prophesied. I cannot compose a new doctrine, because everything the prophets had said was already fulfilled in Christ.”

The law and the prophets had ceased, up to John the Baptist. But John was not the end of the prophets and of the law; Christ was, as the Apostle himself says: “Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.”

### XVI.

“I cannot dig,” he says; “I am ashamed to beg.” It was as though he said: “I, who had been a teacher of the Jews, am forced to beg from uneducated and needy apostles, and from the disciple Ananias, for instruction in salvation and faith!” [Col. 0903C]

Let us open our eyes and see Saul the wolf submit his head to Ananias the sheep. Let us see a man learned in the law receive the teaching of salvation from uneducated men.

Saul knew nothing in the law given by God, because he persecuted Christ, who had given that very law. The uneducated apostles knew the whole law, because they knew Christ as God, who had already fulfilled the law he had given. No human being could fulfill the law except Christ alone, who had given it, as he himself says: “I did not come to abolish the law but to fulfill it.”

If you ask why he is called the unjust steward in relation to the law, which is God’s, let us say: He rightly believed in the Father; in that respect he was a steward. He persecuted the Son; in that respect he was unjust.

A steward is the administrator of a particular estate; hence he received the name *villicus* from *villa*.

From the exalted and proud Saul he became the humble Paul, the chosen vessel of Christ, prepared for every good work. He would not have become a disciple unless he had bowed his neck to an uneducated disciple.

He was also unable to dig a new cistern—that is, to compose a new law. Rather, he opened the cistern that had already been dug and diverted it into rivers: that is, he opened and explained the law that concerned Christ, and he satisfied the arid whole world among the nations when he made them recognize Christ as the Son of God [Col. 0903D].

### XVII.

We ought to follow these examples. Let us not invent things from ourselves, but explain what is written in the law and the Gospel.

And because our Christ is bread in his divinity for the strong and milk in his humanity for the little ones, let us not refuse to provide suitable nourishment to the children of both, according to what each requires, so that what the Lord says in the Gospel may be fulfilled in us: “Who, do you think, is the faithful and wise servant whom the Lord appointed over his household, to give them food at the proper time?”

The wise steward, the pastor of the Church, gives each person food at the proper time, distributing the word of preaching to each in such a way that the soul, gladly receiving it, can take in and carry what he gives.

Otherwise—God forbid—the little one may be suffocated if hard bread is put into his mouth, that is, into speech, where it signifies divinity, without the grinding of teeth.

They must therefore be nourished with milk: they must believe that he is the proper Son of God, not an adopted son; the true God whom the Jews crucified.

He is the true God and eternal life, as the apostle John bears witness when he says: “We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know the true God and be in his true Son Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.”

The apostle Paul says to the Romans: “If God is for us, who is against us? He who did not spare his own Son, but handed him over for us all—how will he not also give us all things with him?”

Again, in the same place: “Their fathers are theirs, and from them, according to the flesh, is Christ, who is God over all, blessed forever.”

And the Lord himself said to the blind man whom he had enlightened: “Do you believe in the Son of God?” He replied: “Who is he, Lord, so that I may believe in him?” Jesus answered him: “You have seen him, and the one speaking with you is he.”

Again, in the Gospel according to John, when he came to raise Lazarus, Martha said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” Jesus said to her: “Your brother will rise.” Martha said to him: “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.” Jesus said to her: “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live; and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

Martha said to him: “Yes, Lord. I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who came into this world” [Col. 0904C].

### XVIII.

We must not therefore doubt concerning him whom the Jews crucified, that he is himself the true, proper Son of God, not an adopted son, but the only Son of God the Father, true God and eternal life.

Let us believe in him—little ones and old, uneducated and wise, poor and rich, men and women. Let every person of every sex die for him so that we may live in him.

Let us worship him without hesitation, because there is no other God besides him, as the prophet Jeremiah bears witness when he says: “This is our God, and no other God exists besides him. He discovered every way of knowledge and gave it to his servant Jacob and to his beloved Israel. After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings” (Baruch 3:36–38).

### XIX.

We must not therefore separate the Father and the Holy Spirit from the Son when we call the Son alone God. The Father and the Son together are one God. The Father alone is not both together, nor is the Son alone both together.

In that highest Trinity, the Father alone is entirely Father in his own person; the Son alone is entirely Son in his own person; and the Holy Spirit alone is entirely Holy Spirit in his own person.

Therefore we neither call the Father the Son, nor impose the name of Father on the Son, nor call the Holy Spirit by the name of Father or Son. In this respect it is truly a Trinity: neither the Father nor the Holy Spirit was born, but the Son alone; neither the Son nor the Holy Spirit begot, but the Father alone; neither the Father nor the Son proceeded from two, but the Holy Spirit alone did so.

Accordingly, the Father alone is God from no God, but from himself. The Son is God, like the Father, but he is God from the Father, not from himself. The Holy Spirit also is God, like the Father and the Son, but he is God from the Father and the Son, not from himself.

The Father alone is God from himself; these two are God from one, that is, from the Father. Thus the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God—not three gods, but one God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

Therefore, when we say in the Scriptures that Christ alone, the Son of God, was born of the Virgin; that the Jews crucified him; that he is true; and that there is no other God besides him, we speak truly, because there is no other God besides him.

For the Father is almighty God and is sufficient in himself in his own person. The Holy Spirit is also almighty God and is sufficient in himself in his own person. Yet these three are not three almighty gods, but one almighty God: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

The Father God alone is sufficient because he cannot be separated from the Son and the Holy Spirit. Christ, the Son of God, is likewise sufficient because he cannot be separated from the Father and the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit too is sufficient because he cannot be separated from the Father and the Son, since the three together are one God [Col. 0905C].

### XX.

Therefore we must not doubt that Christ, the Son of God whom the Jews crucified, is true God and that there is no other God besides him. Let us believe in him and worship him, because there is no other who should be worshiped besides him.

Behold, we have brought forth bread and milk; let each receive as much as he is able. What we say belongs to the Lord, for we who speak are nothing; but he of whom we speak is great, and great is his power, and there is no measure to his wisdom.

He is so great and so excellent that we can neither speak about him nor remain entirely silent about him. Yet although he is indescribable, he must not be unknowable.

Scripture says: “Who will recount his generation?” (Isa. 53:8). It does not say, “Who will fail to know it.” Therefore we must first believe in him, and then we can understand what we read written about him.

For what benefit is there in seeking at peril what can be unknown without peril? It is therefore better to believe what is not understood than to teach what ought to be believed through lying words.

Faith greatly precedes understanding. If faith has merit, and through faith Christ will also give a reward to the uneducated, then faith certainly precedes understanding.

Therefore every uneducated and simple person who rightly believes in Christ, lives simply, and turns away from evil surpasses understanding. Even if understanding appears to possess good works, the uneducated person who has right faith goes before it.

Thus the person who does not believe understands nothing, as the Prophet says: “Unless you believe, you will not understand.”

Therefore, in divine matters, let faith alone be present, and no question will remain. But if you wish to investigate and presume to reason about God and human nature, you will immediately be plunged into the snare of perdition [Col. 0906A].

### XXI.

We must therefore say: We have and worship that God and this human being as one God, with the Father and the Holy Spirit—not a human being, introducing a fourth person—but together with his own flesh we worship the one Christ, the Son of God, who is God, according to the statement of the true faith of the Council of Ephesus, which says:

“We beware of saying concerning Christ: ‘Because of the one who assumed, I venerate the one assumed; and because of the invisible one, I worship the visible one.’”

It is even more horrifying to say this: “The one who was assumed is not called God together with the one who assumed him.”

For whoever says these things divides again into two the one Christ: assigning the human being separately to one part and God likewise separately to another. He plainly denies the unity according to which the one is not worshiped or called together with the other as though they were separate.

Rather, Christ Jesus, the only-begotten Son of God, is understood as one and is to be venerated with one service together with his own flesh.

This is the faith of the first Council of Ephesus, as the text of the Creed also proves.

What, then, can I do for the little ones in mind if, after hearing you, they depart from this unity of faith and confess one Christ as proper according to his divinity but adopted according to his humanity?

What, then, shall we do, we who taught them to hold the apostolic faith, when we ourselves, sucking the breasts of the pure milk of Mother Church, from the law and the Gospel, have by God’s mercy reached the solid food of the divine Trinity?

Let us therefore rise up with the apostles themselves and recite briefly the Creed of our faith which they handed down to us—all of us who have one Lord, one faith, and one baptism. Let us not deny the faith in which we were baptized amid this perversity and duplicity of the heretics.

Rather, as we believe with our heart, let us bring it forth publicly with our own mouth and say:

### XXII.

I believe in God the Father almighty.

And in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our God and Lord, who was born of the Holy Spirit and the virgin Mary.

He suffered under Pontius Pilate.

He was crucified and buried.

He descended to the underworld.

On the third day he rose alive from the dead.

He ascended into heaven.

He sits at the right hand of God the almighty Father.

From there he will come to judge the living and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the forgiveness of all sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and eternal life.

Amen.

### XXIII.

Behold the apostolic faith in which we were baptized, which we believe and hold. If anyone comes to us from other regions, or indeed from our own borders, and brings this faith and this apostolic teaching, let us receive him into the holy Church.

Let us eat and drink with him, because he proclaims peace and is a son of love. Since God is love, and since Christ is the head of the body, the Church, he is a member of the body.

But if anyone does not bring us this faith, attempts to destroy our faith, wishes to mix the leaven of unfamiliar perversity into the unleavened dough of the Church, and causes us scandal, what shall we do with him?

Let us ask the apostle John, the king’s chamberlain, the one who reclined upon the Lord’s breast, the one who drew from his most sacred mouth, from the innermost treasury of the Divinity. The apostle Peter, first among the apostles, also asked him who would betray the Lord.

“Tell us, holy John: what shall we do with this man who disturbs your teaching among us?”

He answers us and says:

“If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house, and do not say ‘Hail’ to him. For whoever says ‘Hail’ to him shares in his evil works.

“For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. Such a person is a deceiver and an Antichrist.

“Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what you have accomplished, but may receive a full reward. Everyone who departs and does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever remains in the teaching of Christ has both the Son and the Father.

“What was from the beginning, what we heard, what we saw with our eyes, what we contemplated, and what our hands touched concerning the Word of life—and the life was manifested, and we saw it and touched it, and we announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and appeared to us—we announce to you what we saw and heard, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and your fellowship may be with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

“Little children, it is the last hour. And just as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, so now many Antichrists have arisen. From this we know that it is the last hour: there are many Antichrists who were with us but are now against us, now outside. They went out from us, but they were not from us. For if they had been from us, they would certainly have remained with us. But this happened so that it might be revealed that not all are from us.

“But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things. I have not written to you as though you did not know the truth, but as those who know it—and because no lie comes from the truth.

“Who is the liar? The one who denies that Jesus is the Christ. This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either. Whoever confesses the Son has the Father” [Col. 0907D].

### XXIV.

“I write these things to you concerning those who lead you astray. And let the anointing that you received from him remain in you. You do not need anyone to teach you; rather, as his anointing teaches you about everything—and it is true and is not a lie—remain in him.

“And now, little children, remain in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not be put to shame by him at his coming.

“But if you know that he is righteous, know also that everyone who practices righteousness has been born from him.

“See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called and should be children of God. For this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know him.

“Beloved, now we are children of God, and it has not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when he appears, we shall see him as he is.

“And everyone who has this hope in him sanctifies himself, just as he is holy.

“Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness, and sin is lawlessness. And you know that he appeared to take away sins, and there is no sin in him.

“Everyone who remains in him does not sin. Everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him.”

### XXV

“Little children, let no one lead you astray. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, just as he is righteous. Whoever commits sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning [Col. 0908B]. For this purpose the Son of God appeared: to destroy the works of the devil. Everyone who has been born of God does not commit sin, but his seed remains in him, and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.

And by this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest. Everyone who is not righteous is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother. For this is the proclamation that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.

Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. Everyone who loves his brother has been born of God and knows God. But whoever does not love his brother does not possess love and does not know God, because God is love.

By this the love of God was manifested among us: God sent his only-begotten Son into the world [Col. 0908C], so that we might live through him. In this is love—not as though we had loved God, but because he loved us and sent his Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.

Beloved, if God loved us, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love is perfected in us.

By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. And we have seen and testify that the Father sent his Son as the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God.

And we have come to know and have believed the love that God has for us. God is love; and whoever remains in love remains in God [Col. 0908D], and God is in him.

By this the love of God is perfected with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so are we in this world. There is no fear in love; rather, perfect love drives out fear, because fear has punishment. Whoever fears, therefore, is not perfected in love.

Let us therefore love God, because God first loved us.”

### XXVI

“If anyone says, ‘I love God,’ and hates his brother, he is a liar. For whoever does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God, whom he does not see? And we have this commandment from him: that whoever loves God must also love his brother.

Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God [Col. 0909A]. And everyone who loves the one who begot him loves the one who has been born from him.

By this we know that we love the Son of God: when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God: that we keep his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome.

For everything that has been born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world: our faith. Who is the one who conquers the world except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

This is he who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not in water only, but in water and blood and flesh. And it is the Spirit who testifies that Christ is the truth.

For there are three who give testimony on earth: water, blood, and flesh. And these three are one. And there are three who give testimony in heaven [Col. 0909B]: the Father, the Word, and the Spirit. And these three are one in Christ Jesus.

If we receive human testimony, the testimony of God is greater. For this is the testimony of God, which is greater: that he has testified concerning his Son, whom he sent as Savior upon the earth. And the Son bore testimony, advancing through the Scriptures; and we bear testimony that we have seen him, and we proclaim him to you, so that you may believe.”

### XXVII

And therefore:

“Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God within him. Whoever does not believe the Son makes him a liar, because he does not believe the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.

And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son of God has life [Col. 0909C]. Whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.

I write these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life—you who believe in the name of the Son of God.

And this is the confidence that we have toward him: that whatever we ask according to his will, he hears us. And we know that he hears us, whatever we ask; we know that we have the requests that we make of him, if we believe in him and love the brothers.

Let us not love as Cain did, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his works were evil, but his brother’s were righteous.

Do not marvel, brothers, if this world hates you. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers [Col. 0909D]. Whoever does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining within him.

By this we know the love of God: that he laid down his life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.

Whoever possesses the substance of this world and sees his brother in need, yet closes his compassion against him—how does the love of God remain in him?”

### XXVIII

“My little children, let us not love in word and tongue only, but in deed and truth. By this we know that we are of the truth, and we persuade our hearts in his presence.

If our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows all things. Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence [Col. 0910A] toward God; and whatever we ask, we shall receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what is pleasing in his sight.

And this is his commandment: that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us commandment. Whoever keeps his commandment remains in him, and he in him. And by this we know that he remains in us: from the Spirit whom he gave us.

Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this the Spirit of God is recognized: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God. And every spirit that dissolves Jesus is not from God.

And this is the spirit of that Antichrist, whom you heard was coming [Col. 0910B] and who is now in the world.

You are of God, little children, and you have conquered them, because the one who is in us is greater than the one who is in the world. They are of the world; therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them. We are of God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not of God does not listen to us. By this we recognize the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.”

### XXIX

This letter, which we have read to your charity, is by John the apostle and evangelist, addressed to the Gentiles. And because we are from the Gentiles, it was addressed to us.

And because the virgin Mary gave birth to Jesus, it concerns Jesus; and because our discussion concerns Jesus, and the Church has been divided into two parties solely on his account, let us examine these two Christs and discover, through the Spirit [Col. 0910C], whose son Jesus is.

He received this name from the Father through the prophet, before he was born of the virgin, when he was announced to the world: “My son Jesus will be revealed to you,” he says.

The angel Gabriel announced this name to the Virgin, saying: “Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever; and of his kingdom there will be no end.”

But Mary said to the angel: “How will this happen, since I do not know a man?” And the angel answered and said to her: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one who will be born from you will be called the Son of God.”

Behold, the Virgin did not doubt the divine command, but she mentioned twice how it would happen [Col. 0910D]. Behold whose son Jesus is!

Let us now see whether he himself is the Lord of heaven and earth. And Mary said: “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word” (Luke 1:38).

She calls herself a handmaid, although she is chosen to be a mother. It is not customary for mothers to call their sons lords; but the Virgin alone, who gave birth to the Lord of heaven and earth, did so.

### XXX

Now Mary rose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, to a city of Judah. She entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. And when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the infant leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. She cried out with a loud voice and said: “And from where is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?”

Behold two witnesses! The Virgin said: “Behold the handmaid [Col. 0911A] of the Lord.” Elizabeth said: “The mother of my Lord.” Both the Virgin and the woman confessed the Lord of heaven and earth.

When ten months had passed, the Virgin gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for her in the lodging.

The angel of the Lord appeared to the shepherds, saying: “Do not be afraid. For behold, I announce to you great joy, which will be for all the people: because today a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.”

For in the Latin language Jesus means “Savior,” but in Hebrew [the name is] Jesus. And suddenly there appeared with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.”

### XXXI

Let us now inquire what this earth [Col. 0911B] is that he has made peaceful. Let us pray to him, and may he who is the truth open our mouth, so that we may speak the truth about him; and may he open the ears of the heart, so that all who hear may understand what we shall say.

If we ask everyone, “From where was Adam made?”—if one person among many speaks and says, “He was made from earth”—there is no doubt, among Jews or Gentiles, Christians or others, that he truly was from earth. And to Adam himself the Lord said in condemnation: “You are earth, and to earth you will go.”

Let us proceed through the sequence of Christ’s genealogy up to the Flood, where Noah alone in that generation was found righteous. Because of his righteousness, seven persons were granted to him, and through him they escaped the Flood.

Just as Jesus Christ alone was found righteous in this world, to whom seven Churches were granted, which escaped the second flood, that of fire [Col. 0911C].

Let us proceed from Noah to Abraham, to whom the first promise was made: that in his seed, which is Christ Jesus, all the nations would inherit.

Let us proceed from Abraham to David, to whom it was said: “From the fruit of your womb I will place one upon your throne.” And: “A rod shall go forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root” (Isaiah 11:1).

The rod from the root of Jesse is the Virgin Mary. The flower from the rod is Jesus Christ, the Son of God. For he says: “I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys.”

Behold: Adam from earth, Noah from Adam, Abraham from Noah, David from Abraham, the Virgin Mary from David, and Jesus Christ, the Son of God, from Mary.

This is: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace” (Luke 2:14). That earth was exalted when it was joined to the Word [Col. 0911D].

Thus the Word made flesh is one Jesus Christ, one person, God and man, just as your soul and flesh are one man. Thus Jesus Christ, the Son of God, God-man, was born from the virgin in the manner in which the soul is taught to be born together with the body. This is not because the two have one substance, but because in both there is one person.

### XXXII

Before our Redeemer was born in the flesh, we were at enmity with the angels. We were far removed from their brightness and purity because of the merit of the first sin and because of our daily transgressions.

Since by sinning we were strangers to God, the angels, who are citizens of God, counted us strangers to their fellowship. But because we came to know our king, the angels recognized their fellow citizens.

Because the King of heaven [Col. 0912A] assumed the earth of our flesh, that angelic exaltation no longer despises our weakness. The angels return to peace with us; they set aside their former purpose of discord. And those whom they previously despised as weak and outcast, they now honor as companions, when they perceive our nature shining with immortal glory in the Lord’s seat.

Certainly, it is that nature which heard: “You are earth, and to earth you will go.” The human nature must rejoice because the earth of our mortality was so assumed by the only-begotten Word that it was established as immortal in heaven, and the earth was so exalted that incorruptible dust returned to the right hand of the Father.

And this is what the angels and the whole Church cry out: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will” (Luke 2:14).

“Of good will” [Col. 0912B] means those who will what is good: those who believe rightly, so that they may be joined with the angels—not those who believe wrongly, so that they may be condemned with the devil.

### XXXIII

When the eight days had been completed for the Lord’s circumcision, his name was called Jesus—the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb (ibid., verse 21).

If we examine the custom of women, it is said of no woman, “She conceived in the womb,” because they received [the seed] externally from men. If we examine the Scriptures, this conception was promised when it was said to the serpent in paradise: “I will place enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed” (Genesis 3:15).

And we rightly understand that women do not have seed and cannot conceive without male seed. Therefore the seed of the woman is the Word [Col. 0912C] made flesh, who is not from earth but from on high, just as Jesus himself says: “I am from above; you are from below.”

And the apostle Paul says: “The first man was from earth, earthly; the second man was from heaven, heavenly.”

When the days of her purification had been completed according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.”

Let us inquire which male opened his mother’s womb. For if we consider the matter correctly, in the case of all women who first had male children, their husbands open the womb—the womb of the woman who alone conceived in the womb.

### XXXIV

When his parents [Col. 0912D] brought the child Jesus into the temple to do for him according to the custom of the law, Simeon took him in his arms, blessed God, and said:

“Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all peoples.”

We have already said above that Jesus is the name of salvation, that is, “Savior.” And he was given as a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for the glory of his people Israel.

And Simeon said to Mary his mother: “Behold, this one is appointed for the fall and resurrection of many in Israel.”

He is plainly appointed for the fall of those who do not believe, and is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense. But for those who believe he is resurrection and life.

“And as a sign that will be opposed” (Luke 2:34).

You see that he is a sign that will be opposed [Col. 0913A]. What is this sign that will be opposed except the cross, the passion, spitting, insults, bonds, blows, slaps, nails, the bitterness of gall, death, the spear, and burial?

As the Lord himself also announced the sign of his death: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature for three days and three nights…”

This is in the sign [alternate reading: “This is the sign”] that will be opposed. These things cause scandal to unbelievers—not only to Jews but also to heretics. They do not wish to apply these things to God, the Son of God.

And therefore they say: “The man Christ, who was born from the Virgin, is called Jesus Christ.” And whoever denies that this man is the Son of God is, according to John, the Antichrist.

### XXXV

Why have we said all this? Because John [Col. 0913B], who gave us this teaching, himself told us: “He has conquered the world who believes that Jesus is the Son of God.”

Jesus has this name as his proper name, and the Gospel repeatedly speaks it, as it says: “Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples,” and so forth.

And when the Jews seized him, he asked them whom they were seeking. They answered: “Jesus the Nazarene.” Then Jesus said to them: “I am he.” And one of those who mocked him struck Jesus with a slap.

And Pilate questioned Jesus. He released Barabbas, but handed Jesus over to them, after he had been scourged, so that they might crucify him. And Jesus cried out with a loud voice on the cross. And Jesus died.

And Jesus the Nazarene whom you seek rose from the dead. And Jesus came through closed doors and stood in the midst of the disciples [Col. 0913C], and said to them: “Peace be with you.”

And he raised his hands, blessed them, departed from them, and was carried into heaven. And every tongue shall confess that Jesus is in the glory of God the Father, to whom, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, belongs one and equal glory.

In faith in him we have already confessed above the teaching that we received from the apostles.

### XXXVI

I believe in God the almighty Father, and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our God and Lord, who was born of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary.

By these three statements [lacuna] nearly all heretics are destroyed. The apostle John confirmed this teaching for us and urged us concerning how we should drive heretics away from us, saying:

“If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house, and do not say ‘greetings’ to him. For whoever says [Col. 0913D] ‘greetings’ to him shares in his evil works.”

Let no one say “greetings” to him—that is, let no one say “rejoice,” or anything else that is customary in greeting.

The true faith, which was handed down by the apostles, is brief. It is without the philosophy of the world; it is simple and manifest to all country people, known to all captives and foreigners. And, to speak more fully, it has been publicly established for the whole Church constituted throughout the world.

It has gathered together in a brief creed how each person should believe. It has also established how one should pray; and the Lord’s Prayer itself is brief. It consists of seven petitions, handed down by the Lord himself as the way in which all believers ought to pray.

Therefore we have nothing to believe beyond the creed, nor anything to pray beyond the Lord’s Prayer. Nor is there anything new—except this new [Col. 0914A] thing, that the Virgin gave birth to God as man: “For the Lord has created a new thing upon the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.”

### XXXVII

As for how we ought to live, that common proverb is sufficient for us: “What you do not want done to you, do not do to another, and you will have eternal life” (Tobit 4:16).

It is common because the common people can say it. The Lord, moreover, says in the Gospel: “Whatever you wish people to do to you, do likewise to them.”

And this is the Church, and Christ. The country person believes rightly because he constantly recites the creed. He prays rightly because he constantly recites the Lord’s Prayer and says: “Our Father, who are in heaven.”

And he is truly a son of God if he does not do to another what he does not wish done to himself.

In that letter of the most holy John we have recited nothing other than what we have told you in rustic and brief [Col. 0914B] speech. For although, according to the Apostle, we are unskilled in speech, we are nevertheless not unskilled in knowledge, by God’s mercy.

Nor are we ashamed of our lack of formal learning, because we are not taught by reading. Nor, in our simplicity, do we doubt the true faith among philosophers, since we have simple and rustic apostles as our teachers.

No philosopher of the world was the first to say, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God,” but Peter the fisherman, a rustic and poor man whose hand was calloused from his work.

This fisherman and rustic went from Jerusalem to Rome. And the rustic conquered Rome, which eloquent men could not conquer.

No worldly wise man was first able to say: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God [Col. 0914C]. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made. And we saw his glory, the glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.”

“And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us”—that is, God became man; and he dwelt among us, that is, he dwelt in the flesh, which we are.

Unless John, a fisherman and rustic, had said this—the John whose letter we have read to you—how would we believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and be one person with him, if we possessed love of God and neighbor?

This is the Church: in love and through love, which is God, so that we may remain in God and God in us, if we do for our neighbor what we want done for ourselves.

For whoever hates his brother is a murderer; and such a murderer does not have eternal life, which is [Col. 0914D] Jesus Christ, as the Apostle says: “That they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.”

He is the true God and eternal life.

Behold our faith: how we believe and pray. We rustic men set it forth briefly to the wise. Teach us, if you know something more.

For, as we have said, the faith is brief. Isaiah himself bears witness to this, saying: “I have heard of matters completed and abbreviated, because the Lord will make a brief word upon the earth” (Isaiah 10:23).

But concerning the one of whom the same prophet prophesied: “Behold, the word of the Lord became a curse for them, and they did not want it.”

Who are those who did not want it except the Jews and heretics, who do not believe that the abbreviated Word—that is, the one made man—is the Son of God, the very one who was wounded for us so that he might heal our wounds?

Concerning him Psalm 106 [Col. 0915A] says: “He sent his Word and healed them, and rescued them from their destruction.”

And this is the word of faith that we preach briefly: “A child has been born for us; a son has been given to us.”

Whose son is this except the Son of God, the true God? He was born for us from the Virgin, not for himself. He was given to us for redemption, not to himself.

“And sovereignty was made upon his shoulders,” because he hung on the cross for us, not for himself. And he was judged for us, not for himself.

For he conquered the prince of death, the devil, when he was judged and condemned to death, so that through death he might destroy the one who held the power of death, as the prophet David bears witness: “And may you conquer when you are judged.”

And this is “sovereignty upon his shoulders.”

And because he is the true God, and there is no other God besides him; hear [Col. 0915B] what follows: “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Mighty, Father of the age to come, Prince of Peace” (Isaiah 9:6).

Behold, we have stated six of his names. According to our faith, which we believe, none of these names belongs to another God besides him.

And if anyone says that the names we have mentioned are not names of Christ, let him hear what follows:

“His dominion shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of his peace. He shall sit upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and strengthen it in judgment and righteousness, from this time forth and forever.”

### XXXVIII

We have set forth our faith to our Church. Let the lord Elipandus now set forth his faith to his Church—the faith in which he rebukes us, so that we may believe by hearing, or, if we are unwilling, be regarded as exiles from his diocese [Col. 0915C].

Then that letter was read. It was greatly contrary to our faith, and its contents had not been written either in the Old Testament or in the New. We gathered together [editorial reading: *quae*, “which”] into one statement the very words of his faith, unfamiliar to us; and, so that they might be more easily recognized, we composed them on the page in a brief summary, in the manner of a creed.

And to show how much it differed from our faith, we set against it the creed of the Council of Ephesus [rather, read: Nicaea].

### XXXIX

I, Hetherius, the unworthy-named bishop of the see of Osma, whom the archbishop of Toledo calls a heretic, am the first to set forth my faith before all who hear.

This faith I received from the holy Fathers, believed, and proclaimed for recitation [Col. 0915D] by the whole Church. And just as I hold it in my heart together with the entire Catholic Church, I state it openly:

“We believe in one God, the almighty Father, maker of heaven and earth, creator of all things visible and invisible.

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born from the Father before all ages: God from God, light from light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, of one substance with the Father—that is, of the same substance as the Father.

Through him all things were made, those in heaven and those on earth. For us and for our salvation he descended. And he was incarnate from the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary and became man.

He suffered under Pontius Pilate. He was buried. On the third day he rose again. He ascended into heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father. He will come again in [Col. 0916A] glory to judge the living and the dead, and his kingdom will have no end.

We believe also in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, proceeding from the Father and the Son, to be worshiped and glorified together with the Father and the Son, who spoke through the prophets.

In one catholic and apostolic Church. We confess one baptism for the remission of sins. We await the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come. Amen.”

**Here ends the creed of the faith of Ephesus.**

## THE CREED OF THE ELIPANDIAN FAITH BEGINS

### XL

“I, Elipandus, archbishop of the see of Toledo [Col. 0916B], together with all who agree with me, believe in the Trinity of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in one essence and nature of the Godhead—that is, God, the Beginning, and the Holy Spirit—in one nature of the Godhead, a Trinity of persons.

For just as a man, when he leaves father and mother and clings to his wife, although they are two persons, are now no longer two but are called one flesh; and just as the souls of many people become one heart and one soul through the love of God, so the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—the maker of the one whole created creation—are an eternal substance, one bond of love, one sphere of affection.

The Father himself also descended by himself to the tower that the sons of Adam were building and said to the Son and the Holy Spirit: ‘Come, let us descend [Col. 0916C] and confuse their languages.’

He also came by himself and rescued Lot from the judgment of Sodom. He likewise descended by himself upon Mount Sinai and gave the law to Moses.

Now if you wish to understand the persons and how God the Trinity is one, observe comparatively the stone and the fire that is in it, with the cold remaining in the stone, and understand that they are one substance.

Consider the comparison of this stone as an undivided Trinity of persons; and, if you are able, contemplate the ineffable Godhead and see the invisible Trinity of one Godhead.

And just as the person of the cold remaining in the stone is one, and the person of the fire remaining in its source is another, yet the fire proceeding forth does not cease to be with the one generating it, so the person of the Son is another, yet does not cease to be with the Father [Col. 0916D] in one substance of the Godhead.

And just as the stone precedes the fire remaining in it in visible appearance, so the Father precedes the Son—not in time but in origin.

The Son of God himself, since he is the radiance of glory and the form of his substance, emptying the invisible Godhead, appeared in the form of subject creation, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, to Abraham in the heat of the day.

For just as the absence of light is darkness, and the absence of darkness is believed to be light, with no third thing intervening between the two, so in the one Word of God, that is, in his only Son, we believe strength, honor, and glory to exist.

And just as the spirit is a part of the soul through which images of bodily things are imprinted; just as the mind is a part of that same soul through which all reasoning and understanding are perceived; and just as memory is that by which one remembers meditating, so in the Word [Col. 0917A] of God different names have been earned according to their functions, though they are in no way divided in substance.

Holy Scripture testifies that, for the salvation of the human race, he emptied his divinity and became man: circumcised, baptized, scourged, crucified, dead, buried, a servant, a captive, a stranger, leprous, despised, and—what is worse—said to have been made lower not only than angels but also than human beings, called a worm, as Scripture says in his person:

‘I am a worm and not a man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people.’

The heavenly beings marvel at his glory according to divinity, and earthly things tremble at his greatness. And he who says, ‘I will not give my glory to another’—the inner man [or: among us], gathered into one and the same person of God and man and clothed in the garment of flesh [Col. 0917B].

For he did not create visible things through the one who was born of the Virgin, but through the one who is not so by adoption but by generation, and not by grace but by nature.

### XLI

“And through this Son of God and man—adoptive in humanity and in no way adoptive in divinity—he redeemed the world.

He is God among gods. Whether he ate or drank remains known to him who did not wish [or: who wished] him to be ignorant of certain mysteries of his activity.

For if all the saints are conformed to this Son of God according to grace, then surely, with the adoptive one there are adoptive ones; with the advocate, advocates; with Christ, christs; with the little one, little ones; and with the servant, servants.

I also believe, among the very gifts of grace of the Holy Spirit, that the Holy Spirit is adoptive [Col. 0917C], in whom we cry, ‘Abba, Father.’ In that Spirit I do not deny that the man Christ is adoptive.

For we believe that in the resurrection we shall be like him—not in divinity, but in the humanity of the flesh, namely, in the assumption of the flesh that he received from the Virgin.”

### XLII

Behold two creeds exceedingly opposed to one another and greatly unlike each other. And these two men, divided on the basis of them, undertake to direct the Church of Christ.

And in accordance with what the apostle John urged us in his letter, saying:

“Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into this world. By this the Spirit of God is recognized. Every spirit that confesses [Col. 0917D] that Jesus has come in the flesh is from God. And every spirit that dissolves Jesus is not from God. And this is the spirit of that Antichrist, whom you heard was coming and who is now already in the world” (1 John 4:3).

What is it to dissolve Jesus except to preach God separately and man separately?

He unquestionably dissolves Jesus who preaches to the people, saying:

“Did he create visible and invisible things through the one who was born of the Virgin, or through the one who is not so by adoption but by generation, and not by grace but by nature, who created all things?”

And therefore, without doubt, he created all things through the one whom [Col. 0918A] he begot as equal to himself and without adoption. And through that Son of God and man, the Word made flesh, adoptive in humanity and in no way adoptive in divinity, he redeemed the world.

Observe the spirit that dissolves Jesus. Open your eyes: the matter is clear. The spirit of error dictated this. The spirit of that Antichrist inspired this.

If this is indeed so, who are those who disagree with the creed, who disagree with the letter? Read John’s letter: it does not say this. But what does it say? “The Antichrist is the one who dissolves Jesus.” It is the spirit of error that denied that Jesus came in the flesh.

The Apostle cries out openly and says: “We have seen and testify that the Father sent his Son as the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God.”

And do we still [Col. 0918B] hesitate to believe? Do we still hesitate to confess?

The Apostle says: “Whoever denies that Jesus is the Son of God denies that he came in the flesh; and he himself is the Antichrist.”

## ELIPANDUS SPEAKS

### XLIII

“Whoever does not confess Jesus Christ as adoptive in humanity and in no way adoptive in divinity is both a heretic and must be exterminated. Remove the evil from your land.

They do not question me but seek to teach, because they are servants of the Antichrist.

I therefore sent this letter of the lord Bishop Ascaricus to your fraternity, dearest Fidelis, so that you may recognize how great humility reigns among the servants of Christ, and how great pride reigns among the disciples of the Antichrist.”

[Note: Col. 0917D. Ascaricus was bishop of Braga; his letter to Elipandus is read in the *Spanish Martyrology*, volume I, page 187.]

“Since the lord Ascaricus wished me to write these things at his request—not under the authority of one who was teaching me, [Col. 0918C] but at the petition of one who was asking questions—as true humility instructed him. But these men, sometimes speaking one thing and its opposite, and sometimes—as though I were ignorant of what was right—not wishing to ask questions but to teach, did not wish to question me. Therefore God knows that, although they wrote presumptuously, if they had spoken the truth I ought gratefully to have obeyed, remembering what is written: ‘If something is revealed to a younger man, the elder keeps silent.’ And again: [Note: [Col. 0917D] This is from Cato.] ‘He is closest to God who knows how to keep silent rationally.’ For it has never been heard of that the Libanenses should teach the Toletans. It is known to the whole people that this see has shone with holy teachings from the very beginning of the faith, and that nothing schismatic has ever proceeded from it. And now, one diseased sheep, you seek to be our teacher. Yet I did not wish [Col. 0918D] to bring these matters to the ears of our other brothers before this sort of evil had been completely uprooted there, where it first arose. For it will be a disgrace to me if [Note: [Col. 0918D] Perhaps: within the jurisdiction of Toledo.] this evil is heard of in the Toletan tradition, so that what I and my other brothers have judged for so long among the people of Seville, and, with God’s help, have corrected—both in the observance of Easter festivals and in the other errors [Note: [Col. 0918D] They differed from the others concerning the celebration of Easter. Accordingly, they were condemned by the Council of Seville, presided over by Elipandus, bishop of Toledo.]—of the Migetian heresy, they now, on the contrary, find grounds on which to accuse us. Yet if the matter is handled negligently and is not corrected by you, then I shall bring it to the attention of the brothers [Col. 0919A], and it will be disgraceful for you if it is reproved in you by those men.”

### XLIV

“Your fraternity should instruct the youth of our brother Heterius, still nourished on milk and not yet brought to the strength of mature understanding, because he held a conference not with excellent teachers but with ignorant and schismatic men—namely, Felix and Beatus [Note: [Col. 0919D] Antiphrasius; for Elipandus called Beatus by this name by antiphrasis, as is also clear from Charlemagne’s letter to Elipandus. STEW.] Atiphrasius—equal in virtue and alike in error. Bonosus and Beatus were condemned for the same error. The former believed that Christ was adoptive from his mother, and not truly begotten from the Father before the ages, and that he was not adoptive from his mother in time. Whom shall I consider like him, except Faustus the Manichaean? Faustus condemned the patriarchs and prophets; this man condemns the ancient and modern teachers. I beg you, kindled by the heat of faith and fervent in such earnestness, to remove the aforesaid error from your midst, so that, just as the Lord through his servants uprooted the Migetian heresy from the regions of Baetica, so through you he may tear out the Beatian heresy completely from the regions of the Asturians. But since I have heard that the precursor of Antichrist has appeared in your midst, announcing that he has already been born, I ask you to inquire of him where, or how, or when that lying spirit of the prophets was born, the spirit that speaks in him, and to make us concerned [Florez: ‘make us concerned’].”

### XLV

This is your letter. These are your words. This is your faith. This is your teaching. This is your wisdom. And you command us to bow to them. And because we do not bow, you shout that we are heretics [Col. 0919C] and precursors of Antichrist. And that same lying spirit who entered the mouth of Ahab’s prophets speaks in us. And you say to your Fidelis: “Inquire where he was born, and make us concerned.” This insult is directed not against us but against the very one whom we worship. Yet if we rightly believe in the Son of God, as we believe the truth without hesitation, the insult against him is also an insult against us. And when it is an insult against him, it is ours, because head and body are one person. For when the foot is trampled, the head is not glorified.

### XLVI

Indeed, the Head had already ascended to heaven when Saul was slaughtering Christ’s disciples. And it was said to him: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?” He did not say, “Why are you persecuting my servants?” but, “Why are you persecuting me?” [Col. 0919D]

Peter too, the first of the apostles, out of compassion for the weeping disciples, so as not to abandon them but to depart from the city and flee before Nero, overcome by the disciples’ tears, yielded and promised that he would leave the City. [Note: [Col. 0919D] Ambrose likewise relates this in *Against Auxentius, On the Basilica* [Col. 0920D]—not transmitted; Hegesippus, book III, chapter 2; Gregory, *On Psalm IV, of Penance*; Cardinal Baronius, under the year A.D. 69, *Ecclesiastical Annals*.]

On the following night, after greeting the brothers and celebrating prayer, he began to set out alone. When he had come to the gate, he saw Christ coming to meet him. He worshiped him and said: “Lord, where are you going?” Christ said to him: “I am coming again to be crucified.” He understood that this referred to his own passion: Christ appeared to be suffering in him, since he suffers in each one—not, of course, through bodily pain, but through a certain compassion of mercy or through the renown of glory. Peter immediately turned back into the city; and, having been seized by his persecutors, he was condemned to the cross.

Paul himself, the vessel of election, tells the disciples: “Every day I complete in my flesh what is lacking in Christ’s sufferings.” And because there are two kinds of martyrdom—that is, suffering and compassion—the Lord suffered in Peter and James, and he showed compassion in John. Concerning James and John he said: “Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They answered: “We can.” Jesus said to them: “You will drink my cup.” And certainly, when a cup is mentioned in Scripture, it signifies suffering.

For every servant of God who has the right faith—for “the righteous person lives by faith”—and who loves every human being as himself, drinks Christ’s cup. This is not openly the shedding of blood or the suffering of the body, but compassion of the soul. For each drinks one and the same cup of Christ, as Solomon says in the *Song of Songs*: “Love is strong as death” (Song of Songs VIII, 6). Just as the one who dies no longer sees this world, so the one who loves every human being as himself cannot see this world—that is, the lovers of the world.

Such a person can say with the apostle Paul: “Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I am not burned?” For wherever tribulation or heresy arose in the Church, he was immediately afflicted and at once suffered with each person, like Christ, who suffers in each one—not, of course, through bodily pain, but through compassion of the soul. This suffering and compassion are one suffering, because the cup that is drunk is one, and the head and body that suffer are one person.

I do not see how one who says that he rightly believes in Christ can rightly believe in him while refusing to receive his members. For one who hates a human being does not love the whole Christ. And everyone who hates his brother is Cain, a fratricide, a murderer. Such a murderer does not have Christ, who is eternal life. He does not have Christ because he does not imitate Christ; he would imitate him if he loved every human being as himself—and not only friends, but enemies as well: friends in God, and enemies for God’s sake.

For Christ died not for friends but for enemies. He loved his enemies so greatly that he handed himself over to death for them. If he had not done so, no one would be found to praise him. But while we were enemies, he died for us, leaving us an example so that we might follow his footsteps.

The apostle John says: “Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.” “In this we know the love of God: that he laid down his life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.”

Why have we said all this, except to establish what the Church is? And when the Church is recognized, Christ too is recognized, for he is the [Col. 0921A] head of the Church. And where the Church of Christ is, there is peace, because Christ is our peace, he who made both himself and us one.

### XLVII

Therefore we preach love, and we wish to have no occasion of stumbling with anyone, according to the prophet’s saying: “Great peace have those who love your law, and there is no stumbling-block for them.” You, then, who have a grievance against us, say why.

Here the Lord says in the Gospel: “They will not cease to come, so that scandals may arise; woe to that person through whom the scandal comes” (Matthew XVIII, 7). Let us seek the origin of this scandal, from where it arose; and, according to the Lord’s saying, woe will be to the one through whom it came.

You wrote a new teaching and abandoned that which is proclaimed throughout the whole world by the voice of all the baptized. And because your teaching was unknown to us, we did not wish to accept it and abandon that which the Church throughout the whole world holds. Behold the source from which the scandal came into the Church. Woe to the one through whom it came.

For our faith is the Creed, and upon this stands the Catholic Church established throughout the whole world. It is believed to be spread abroad, not divided. But you composed a new creed, one not found in the sacred Scriptures, and sent it into our Church, so that we should believe in the Trinity of the persons of the Father and the Son in one nature, the same being. Sabellius said this as well. For he said that the Father and the Son were merely names in one God, together with the Holy Spirit; nevertheless, he confused the persons by saying that they were one person.

Just as one human being has one nature, and in him there is an image of the Trinity—namely, memory, understanding, and will—which are three in one nature and one person and one human being, and yet those three are not the human being itself: this is what I have said about the Trinity in the one God, so that we may believe in the Trinity of the persons of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit in one nature, that is, in one God.

And because one human being is an image of the Trinity in the soul, so too are memory, understanding, and will. Those three are in the one person of the human being, yet they are not the human being; rather, the whole is one person. Thus you compel us to understand and believe that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are in one God, in one nature, and that those three are not themselves God, just as the three we mentioned above are not themselves the human being.

But if we are not speaking the truth, let spiritual men examine the matter; those who read books on the Trinity cannot discover that we believe anything else. Yet because the subject is extensive and must be examined in detail, we ought to bring forward the matters from which the scandal arose, on account of which we have received from you the name of schismatics and heretics.

### XLVIII

We have already spoken of your Trinity, which we do not accept. Let us also speak of your Christ, whom we do not believe to be such as you claim. For you say:

“Did he who was born of the Virgin create the visible and invisible things through that same person, or did he who is not adoptive but natural, and not by grace but by nature, create all things? Therefore, without doubt, he created many things through him whom he begot equal to himself and without adoption. And through this Son of God and man, the Word made flesh, adoptive in humanity and in no way adoptive in divinity, he redeemed the world.”

[Col. 0922A]

### XLIX

Behold your faith concerning Christ. We do not accept it, because we possess neither such a faith nor such a teaching received from the apostles, nor have we ever read anything of the kind in the Law or the Gospel, or in the books of the teachers or in the manuals, but only in your dogmas.

For this reason we are called by you disciples of Antichrist. Behold the source from which the scandal arose between us. You said many other things, which we included above in your creed; but they are not now to be examined, because we are not capable of doing so. Yet if God wills and we live, they must be examined and rejected by the Church—God forbid that through them we should lose the Christian name and henceforth bear not the name of Christians but of Elipandians.

Whoever follows someone’s faith takes that person’s name, just as the Arians are named from Arius, the Sabellians [Col. 0922B] from Sabellius, and the others from the names of their founders. Therefore one Christ, the Son of the Virgin, who bears the name Jesus, is sufficient for us.

We have no need of those of yours whom you call “this one” and “that one,” because we do not recognize the names of those persons written by you. You said “this one” and “that one,” but you could not name Jesus, because you did not have him in your heart. If you had had him, you could have said with the apostle Paul: “Do you seek proof of the Christ who speaks in me?” And elsewhere he says that no one can say “Lord Jesus” except in the Holy Spirit.

Indeed, even in his Letters he did not dare to say with you, with divinity emptied: “We are adoptive, and he is adoptive; we are Christs, and he is Christ; we are little ones, and he is a little one,” and the other filth that you dared to say about Jesus Christ our Lord, making him a servant among servants.

But his Letter to the Romans reads as follows:

“Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Gospel of God, which he had promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy Scriptures concerning his Son, who was made from the seed of David according to the flesh, who was predestined to be the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of sanctification through the resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord; through whom we have received grace and apostleship for obedience to the faith among all the nations, among whom you also are called by Jesus Christ; to all the saints who are in Rome, beloved of God, called as saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

“First, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world. For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of his Son.”

Whose servant did the apostle Paul say he was? And in whose Son’s Gospel did he serve? Open your eyes and see the poison. Cast it out quickly, lest you die from it.

Read all of Paul’s Letters, and you will find him calling himself the servant of Jesus Christ and confessing the Son of God openly before everyone. For you will not find there “this one” and “that one,” adoptive in humanity and in no way adoptive in divinity.

Read the seven catholic epistles: the two of the apostle Peter, the three of the apostle John, and the single epistles of Jude and James; this will not be found written there. Read the four books of the Gospels, the Apocalypse of John, and the Acts of the Apostles, and [Col. 0923A] you will not find this there either. Rather, you will find them calling themselves servants of Jesus Christ and affirming him to be the true God, the Son of God.

Read the books of all the teachers, down to the manuals, and you will find that no one wrote such things, because no one believed such things. But if you truly find written there anything like what was recently written by Elipandus, bishop of the Toletan see, then believe him when he says that we are heretics and disciples of Antichrist, and drive us from your land; and, according to his command, remove the evil from your midst.

But if we speak the truth, he speaks falsehood, because we do not have one faith. And a divided [diverse] faith does not produce one charity; therefore the Church has been divided into two parts. And now, girded with the weapons of the Scriptures, each of us has openly risen to battle in defense of his faith.

And because three kings have risen against one, let us not be afraid. Be strong: for those who are with us are more numerous than those who are with them.

### L

With us is that strong-handed David, who struck the blasphemous Goliath—who reproached the army of the God of Israel—with a small stone on the forehead and felled him with a single blow.

With us is Moses, who drowned Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea and made his people cross on dry foot.

With us is Joshua, who shut five kings in one cave, and who had previously defeated Amalek.

With us is Father Abraham with three hundred household servants, who overcame five kings and stripped them of their spoils—for these men are only three kings.

With us is the very mighty Gideon, and three hundred chosen men with him, with whom he struck Midian as though it were a single man.

With us is Samson, stronger than a lion and harder than a rock, who alone, without weapons, felled a thousand armed men.

With us are the twelve patriarchs. With us are the sixteen prophets, the apostles, and the evangelists. With us are all the martyrs and teachers.

With us is Jesus, the Son of the Virgin, together with the whole Church, purchased with his own blood and spread throughout the world. The enemy is confined and hemmed in only in one corner.

Stand, therefore, according to the Apostle, with your loins girded in truth; put on the breastplate of righteousness; and with your feet shod in readiness for the Gospel of peace. In all things take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one; and take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

Let us say with the most holy prophet David: “Our help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.” He has granted victory to those who fight, he who gave them the courage to fight.

Let neither the multitude of the enemy, nor the appearance of the combatants, nor weapons that seem to glitter like glass terrify or turn us back. “Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will glory in the name of our God.” Let us not be afraid. They are not warriors; they are merchants of the world. They carry on their own business, not ours; they seek their own things, not the things of Jesus Christ.

They claim to carry gold and silver; but it is mixed, adulterated, false. Let the money-changers come and see that it is a lie. Let no one receive anything from them; let no one buy, lest he later regret it.

They offer us wine. Let no one receive it; let no one drink it. It is mixed with water. [Col. 0924A] And what you see here contains more water than wine.

### LI

This too once happened in the time of Jeremiah. There were false prophets—that is, heretics—who proclaimed false and adulterated words to the people and said: “Thus says the Lord,” although the Lord had not sent them at all.

Therefore, through Isaiah, he called them the most loathsome wine-merchants, saying: “Your wine-merchants mix wine with water” (Isaiah I, 22), because they mixed with the wise and unmixed wine—that is, the word of God—something insipid and watered down, namely an earthly and human teaching, as though mixing water into wine, and presented it to the people.

For this reason they deserved to be called wine-merchants who mix water with wine. And although wine is named in this passage, it is nevertheless good, because it is the teaching of the prophets and apostles. But because it is mixed—that is, infected with heretical depravity—this water is not from the true fountain, that is, it is not from the teaching of Christ, but gathered from the heretics’ pool and from the world’s false knowledge.

They color their wisdom with obscure words, understood by few, so that in some manner or other it may be mixed with the true doctrine. We, taught by the Holy Spirit, recognize that spirit of error which devises these things for itself, so that it may assume the name of teacher and join its own teaching, mixed with the Church’s teaching, to it.

Moses turned this water into blood; this was the first plague of Egypt. And although those events took place bodily in Egypt, they now take place spiritually in us. For Egypt is a figure of the world, in whose first plague water is turned into blood.

And all heretics are philosophers, for a rustic cannot be called a heretic. Hence the waters of Egypt will be [Col. 0924C] the slippery and obscure philosophizing doctrine of the heretics. They are rightly turned into blood because they understand the holy Scriptures carnally.

But as soon as the cross of Christ is present, it shows them the light of truth and rebukes them more sharply, so that from the character of the persons they may recognize their particular errors. Then it is proved which spirit is God’s and which is the spirit of error.

### LII

Concerning this spirit of error it is said in the Apocalypse: “And I saw coming from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet three unclean spirits like frogs” (Revelation XVI, 13).

Who else is the dragon except the devil? The beast received its name from devastation, because it does not eat grass but sheds blood and tears flesh, from which it lives. What else is this beast except a human being who crushes another human being [Perhaps: kills him]? The false prophet, however, is the heretic.

He testifies that he saw three spirits, but there is one spirit. For just as a human being who clings to God becomes one spirit, so an evil person, by clinging to a heretic, becomes one spirit with the devil. Thus the devil himself says of himself: “I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the north.”

The devil presides over the mountain of the covenant when he holds the hearts of heretics. The sides of this mountain are all those who consent to them and stand as their defenders.

These spirits are their words, because they speak what the devil inspires in them. The spirit says that they are like frogs. A frog is exceedingly loquacious vanity. For this animal is fit for no food, since it is unclean. It has no other usefulness except that it returns the sound of its voice in wicked and importunate cries; for frogs roll about in pools, mud, and foul collections of water.

So heretics do not emit their voices from the clearest water, the living water that comes from the fountains of the Savior—that is, the teaching of the apostles—but from the ignorant and slippery people themselves, with unworthy cries, like frogs from the mud. By a certain empty and inflated modulation of pride, like the sounds and songs of frogs, they write stories of deception.

### LIII

Thus, while pretending to be pure gold and silver, they seek to deceive us in a business in which they have mixed bronze and tin with the material.

Let us nevertheless become, according to the Lord’s command, approved money-changers, because the discipline of expertise consists in testing what is the purest gold, commonly called *obryzum*, and what is the material less purified by fire, earthy [bronze], and a cheap coin.

If a precious coin is altered by the gleam of shining gold, we must provide against deception with the utmost prudence. We must consider not only whether the gold is pure, but also, examining sharply, whose image it bears—whether that of the true king or of a robber.

For because a robber steals gold, he does not presume to trade it publicly. Instead, he puts it back into the smelting furnace and reproduces the emperor’s face and image under a counterfeit appearance.

This too we must wisely recognize, and with swift discernment determine whether the coin is that of the true king or has been improperly fashioned by a false merchant. And when we see that it is pure gold, without admixture, and bears the image of the true king, we must still hesitate and not purchase it unless it is placed on the balance. We must carefully investigate, lest it be deficient in weight.

### LIV

That all these things must also be observed by us spiritually is demonstrated by the Gospel saying under the form of this example.

First, whatever has crept into our hearts, or whatever new teaching has been introduced, we must test [the spirit] diligently, to determine whether it has been purified by that divine and heavenly fire of the Holy Spirit, or whether it has entered through the spirit of error. If it comes from heretical depravity, or descends from the swelling of secular philosophy, and, bearing hypocrisy under the name of holiness, displays piety only on the surface, we must examine it with the greatest care.

We shall be able to accomplish this if we follow the apostolic command: “Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, to see whether they are from God.”
